2	name: note-conformance
3	description: Audit a note's frontmatter, slug, links, and prose against wakil's schema and output-quality bar, and fix what's mechanical or flag what isn't. Use after drafting or revising a note, or when auditing existing pages for schema/prose drift.
4	skill_api: 1
5	---
6	
7	# note-conformance
8	
9	This is a checking skill, not a content-generating one. `content-synthesis` and
10	`note-revision` decide what a note says; `note-conformance` is the pass that
11	verifies the result is shaped correctly before it goes through `kb-commit` —
12	schema-valid frontmatter, a consistent slug, deterministic links, and prose
13	that meets the no-slop bar. Run it on one note at a time; it produces a short
14	list of fixes applied and issues flagged, not a rewrite.
15	
16	## When to use
17	
18	- After drafting a new note or substantially revising an existing one.
19	- Before `kb-commit`, as a last check on anything about to be written to the
20	  knowledge base.
21	- When explicitly asked to audit existing pages for drift (stale frontmatter
22	  casing, mismatched slugs, missing citations).
23	
24	For frontmatter drift across many notes at once, prefer `wakil schema migrate`
25	(below) over hand-editing every file — let the deterministic tool do the
26	mechanical part, and reserve this skill's judgment for what it can't cover.
27	
28	## Procedure
29	
30	- [ ] Step 1: **Run the mechanical pass first.** For the note's entity type,
31	      run `wakil schema migrate --dry-run --type <type>` and read the diff.
32	      Apply it (`--yes` or per-file confirm) before doing anything by hand —
33	      see "Mechanical fixes" below for exactly what this does and doesn't
34	      cover.
35	- [ ] Step 2: **Check the category rule.** Confirm `name:` vs `title:`
36	      matches the entity's schema category — see "Category rule" below. This
37	      is a hard schema error, not a style preference.
38	- [ ] Step 3: **Check the three-part slug.** Filename, H1, and every
39	      wikilink pointing at this note must agree — see "Slug consistency"
40	      below.
41	- [ ] Step 4: **Check links.** Internal cross-references are `[[path]]`
42	      wikilinks using the note's full workspace-relative path; external
43	      links are copied verbatim from their source, never reconstructed. See
44	      "Links" below.
45	- [ ] Step 5: **Check prose against the no-slop bar.** No filler, no hedged
46	      citations, no LLM preamble, no placeholder dates, exact phrasing
47	      preserved where the phrasing is the insight, titles under 60
48	      characters and specific. See "No-slop output bar" below.
49	- [ ] Step 6: **Report, don't silently resolve, what you can't fix.** A fact
50	      with no traceable source, an entity type unknown to the schema, an
51	      ambiguous frontmatter conflict — flag these explicitly rather than
52	      guessing or deleting. See "Deterministic links, uncitable facts"
53	      below.
54	
55	## Mechanical fixes: `wakil schema migrate`
56	
57	`wakil schema migrate` (`src/wakil/app/schema_migrate_service.py`) is the
58	cheap tier only: mechanical fixes a linter could make, not judgment calls.
59	Concretely, per file, it:
60	
61	- renames casing/naming duplicates (`end_date`→`end-date`, `start_date`→
62	  `start-date`, `linkedin-link`→`linkedin`, `authors`→`author`, `link`→`url`),
63	  dropping the old key only when it's an exact duplicate value — a genuine
64	  conflict (both present, different values) is left in place and surfaced,
65	  never silently resolved;
66	- retypes `organization/`-directory files that were declared `type: concept`
67	  back to `type: organization`;
68	- aligns a mechanically re-cased `title` back to an authored-case `name` when
69	  they differ only by casing (guards a title-caser artifact like `1NSP` →
70	  `1nsp` without touching a genuinely different title);
71	- normalizes a quoted `type: "..."` value.
72	
73	It does **not** touch page structure, section shape, exact-phrasing
74	preservation, or title quality — those stay this skill's prose judgment (see
75	"No-slop output bar"). It also never retypes an unknown `type` or resolves an
76	ambiguous rename; those are always left for manual review.
77	
78	Run it with `--dry-run` first and read the diff before applying — this is
79	`wakil`'s own implementation of test-the-sample-before-the-batch discipline:
80	`plan_schema_migration` only proposes (nothing is touched during planning),
81	and `apply_migrations` re-reads each file immediately before writing,
82	skipping any file that changed on disk since the plan was made rather than
83	overwriting it blind. Use `--type <type>` to scope a run to one entity type,
84	`--yes` to apply without per-file confirmation once you've reviewed the plan,
85	and `--commit` to have each type's fixes land as its own `wakil chore: ...`
86	commit.
87	
88	## Category rule: `name:` vs `title:`
89	
90	The identity/document split is enforced in code
91	(`src/wakil/schema/validate.py:62-69`), not by convention — get it wrong and
92	`validate_frontmatter` returns a hard `SchemaError`, not a warning:
93	
94	- **identity** types (e.g. `person`, `company`) use `name:` only. A `title:`
95	  field on an identity type is an error.
96	- **document** types (e.g. `meeting`) use `title:` only. A `name:` field on a
97	  document type is an error.
98	
99	```yaml
100	# identity type (src/wakil/schema/entities/person.yaml) — name only
101	---
102	type: person
103	name: Jane Doe
104	status: active
105	created: 2026-07-16
106	updated: 2026-07-16
107	---
108	```
109	
110	```yaml
111	# document type (src/wakil/schema/entities/meeting.yaml) — title only
112	---
113	type: meeting
114	title: Q3 planning sync
115	date: 2026-07-16
116	created: 2026-07-16
117	---
118	```
119	
120	An `entity_type` the schema doesn't recognize is itself a hard error — don't
121	best-guess a schema for an unfamiliar `type:`; flag it.
122	
123	## Slug consistency
124	
125	A note's slug appears in three places, and all three must be the same
126	lowercase-kebab string:
127	
128	1. the filename (minus `.md`);
129	2. the H1 heading at the top of the note body;
130	3. every `[[wikilink]]` elsewhere in the knowledge base that points at this
131	   note.
132	
133	`slugify()` (`src/wakil/app/ingest_service.py:661`) is the reference
134	implementation wakil itself uses (and `git_service.py` reuses for branch
135	names): lowercase, non-alphanumeric runs collapsed to a single `-`, leading
136	and trailing `-` stripped. Use it as the definition of "correctly slugged,"
137	not a separate hand-rolled rule. A note whose H1 is Title Case, or whose
138	filename and H1 disagree, is a conformance failure — fix the drifting one to
139	match the filename, don't rename the file to match a stray heading.
140	
141	## Links
142	
143	**Internal cross-references** use the wikilink form `[[path]]`, where `path`
144	is the note's full workspace-relative path — never a bare filename, never a
145	title string, and never a path built relative to the linking file (no
146	`../...`). `schema/validate.py`'s `ref` field kind only checks that a
147	reference is a string; resolving it to an actual note is the knowledge
148	base's own `RESOLVER.md` (a workspace-provided file wakil reads, not one it
149	ships) — defer to whatever path/slug convention the open workspace's
150	`RESOLVER.md` states, but the "absolute path from the vault root, never
151	relative" rule itself is non-negotiable regardless of workspace.
152	
153	**External links** are copied verbatim from their source — see "Deterministic
154	links" below.
155	
156	## No-slop output bar
157	
158	Notes are durable artifacts, not chat output:
159	
160	- No filler phrases ("It's worth noting that...", "Interestingly...").
161	- No hedging when a fact is cited — "X is true" per the source, not "X might
162	  be true."
163	- No LLM preamble ("I've created...", "Here's the updated...", "Certainly!").
164	- No placeholder dates ("recently," an unfilled `YYYY-MM-DD`).
165	- Preserve a speaker's exact words rather than paraphrasing when their
166	  phrasing is itself the insight — don't clean up grammar or swap in your
167	  own terminology for a person's own framework or coinage.
168	- Titles are descriptive enough to find in a search result, under 60
169	  characters, not full sentences, and not generic ("Jane Doe, VP Eng at
170	  Acme" not "Person Page").
171	
172	## Deterministic links, uncitable facts
173	
174	Never guess or reconstruct a URL — a wikilink is built from the note's actual
175	path, an external link is copied from the source that supplied it, never
176	composed from a slug or a memory of what the URL "should" be.
177	
178	When a fact has no traceable source, or a link can't be built deterministically,
179	**flag it rather than inventing a citation or silently deleting the fact.**
180	Both failure modes are worse than an honest gap: a fabricated source misleads
181	every future reader, and a deleted fact is knowledge the base quietly loses.
182

1	---
2	name: ingest-source
3	description: Orchestrate the end-to-end path from raw external material to a committed, linked, conformant knowledge-base note — normalize, capture, enrich, resolve entities, route, and conform — resuming by source id on failure. Use whenever asked to ingest, capture, or process external material into the knowledge base.
4	skill_api: 1
5	---
6	
7	# ingest-source
8	
9	This is the top-level, user-facing workflow. It does not do its own content
10	judgment — it decides which of the six focused skills below apply to the
11	material in front of it, in what order, and gets out of the way once each
12	has done its job. If you catch yourself deciding what a note should say,
13	which entity a mention resolves to, or where a file belongs, stop — that
14	judgment belongs to `content-synthesis`, `entity-resolution`, or
15	`note-routing` respectively, not to this skill.
16	
17	## The two-command backbone
18	
19	For the three shapes `wakil` ingests natively, the whole pipeline is two
20	commands:
21	
22	```text
23	wakil ingest {transcript,text,article}     step 1: capture (deterministic, no model)
24	wakil enrich <source-id>                   step 2: analyze and link (model-driven DAG)
25	```
26	
27	`wakil ingest` writes the raw material under `sources/` and records a
28	`Source` row, nothing more — no interpretation happens at this step.
29	`wakil enrich <source-id>` then runs a fixed, code-sequenced DAG
30	(`src/wakil/app/ingest_service.py`, `prepare_enrichment`):
31	
32	1. **DAG node 1 — extraction.** Runs the CLI-native judgment from the
33	   `transcript`/`text`/`article` skill (this is exactly what
34	   `content-synthesis` describes as already handled for native source
35	   types) and produces a proposed primary note.
36	2. **DAG node 2 — entity resolution.** Always invoked, never optional.
37	   Runs the `entity-resolve` skill (the same judgment `entity-resolution`
38	   documents) and, for every entity it decides to create, writes a
39	   schema-routed stub page via `schema.directory` — the deterministic slice
40	   of what `note-routing` calls "entity types are code-owned."
41	3. **Validation gate.** `validate_proposal()` checks every proposed file
42	   carries schema-valid frontmatter for its `type:` and hard-stops on an
43	   unrecognized type or a duplicate path — a partial, mechanical slice of
44	   what `note-conformance` checks in full.
45	
46	Then one preview, one confirm, one apply. Nothing is written before you
47	confirm; nothing partial is left behind if you decline.
48	
49	## Where the automatic DAG stops — and why this skill exists beyond it
50	
51	The DAG above gives you a schema-valid primary note plus schema-valid entity
52	stubs. It does **not**:
53	
54	- write texture into a stub's State (Compiled Truth), decide which of the
55	  source's *other* mentions earn a back-link, or add Timeline entries beyond what
56	  extraction directly proposed — that's `entity-enrichment`'s job, per its
57	  own description of exactly this gap;
58	- route the primary note through the workspace's `RESOLVER.md` — the
59	  extraction skill picks the proposed note's path itself, so anything that
60	  needs workspace-specific subject-matter placement beyond what the
61	  extraction skill already decided is `note-routing`'s job;
62	- run the full no-slop prose bar, three-way slug consistency, or link-format
63	  audit — only frontmatter schema validity is checked automatically; the
64	  rest is `note-conformance`'s job.
65	
66	So: for material where the automatic stub-and-scaffold output is genuinely
67	sufficient (a minor mention, a low-stakes capture), `wakil enrich` alone may
68	be enough. For anything that matters — a page worth real texture, a note
69	whose placement isn't obvious from the extraction skill's own guess, a
70	result you're about to commit — continue the workflow by hand through
71	`entity-enrichment` → `note-routing` → `note-conformance` before handing the
72	result to `kb-commit`. Use judgment on how far to go; don't assume the DAG's
73	automatic output is the finished product just because it applied cleanly.
74	
75	## Dispatch: does the material need normalizing first?
76	
77	| Material | Path |
78	|---|---|
79	| Meeting/call transcript file (`.txt`, `.md`, `.srt`) | CLI-native — `wakil ingest transcript` directly |
80	| Plain text, pasted note, clipping | CLI-native — `wakil ingest text` directly |
81	| Web article URL | CLI-native — `wakil ingest article` directly |
82	| PDF, voice note, YouTube video, scanned/OCR document, or anything else not already one of the three shapes above | Normalize first via `source-ingestion`, then continue through the same two-command backbone |
83	
84	`source-ingestion` owns all of the per-source-type judgment for the
85	normalize-first column — what to extract, how to classify the result as
86	`transcript` vs. `text`, and how to build a `--context` string rich enough
87	for DAG node 1 to use. Don't re-derive that judgment here; hand the
88	material off and resume once it's normalized.
89	
90	## Full workflow
91	
92	```text
93	source-ingestion            (only when normalization is needed — see dispatch table)
94	        ↓
95	wakil ingest {shape}         capture: writes sources/*, deterministic
96	        ↓
97	wakil enrich <source-id>     DAG: content-synthesis (native judgment)
98	        ↓                         + entity-resolution + schema-valid stubs
99	entity-enrichment            texture, back-links, Timeline beyond the DAG's proposal
100	        ↓
101	note-routing                 placement for anything not already schema-routed
102	        ↓
103	note-conformance             full schema/slug/link/prose audit
104	        ↓
105	kb-commit                    reviewable diff, commit
106	```
107	
108	Each stage's output is distinct, and that separation is the point — a
109	retry at any stage doesn't repeat the stages before it:
110	
111	1. **`source-ingestion`** (conditional) → a normalized transcript/text file
112	   plus a `--context` string, ready for `wakil ingest`.
113	2. **`wakil ingest`** → the raw source note under `sources/`, recorded with
114	   a source id.
115	3. **`wakil enrich`** → a proposed primary note plus schema-valid entity
116	   stubs, previewed and applied together.
117	4. **`entity-enrichment`** → back-links, Compiled Truth texture, and
118	   Timeline entries the DAG didn't generate on its own.
119	5. **`note-routing`** → a destination directory and filename for anything
120	   the DAG's own extraction-skill guess didn't already settle.
121	6. **`note-conformance`** → a note that's schema-valid, consistently
122	   slugged, cleanly linked, and free of slop — ready to commit.
123	7. **`kb-commit`** → the actual commit, with a message and diff the user
124	   can review.
125	
126	## Resuming a failed or interrupted run
127	
128	Track progress by **source id**, not by re-running earlier stages:
129	
130	- Capture is idempotent by content hash — re-running `wakil ingest` on
131	  material already captured reports the existing source id and writes
132	  nothing new. It is safe to re-run, but it does not advance a stalled
133	  pipeline; resume with `wakil enrich <source-id>` instead.
134	- If capture succeeded but `wakil enrich` failed, was declined at the
135	  confirmation prompt, or `validate_proposal()` blocked it on a schema
136	  issue — fix the underlying cause (an unrecognized entity type, a
137	  workspace schema gap) and re-run `wakil enrich <source-id>`. Don't
138	  re-capture; the source already exists.
139	- To re-analyze a source that already completed enrichment (new
140	  information surfaced, the first pass was thin), re-run
141	  `wakil enrich <source-id> --force`.
142	- If enrichment applied but the manual stages (`entity-enrichment`,
143	  `note-routing`, `note-conformance`) haven't run yet, pick up from
144	  whichever of those is next — each is safe to run on the DAG's output
145	  independent of how capture or enrichment went.
146	
147	## Committing
148	
149	`wakil ingest`/`wakil enrich` can commit their own output directly via
150	`--commit`/`--branch`/`--pr`, using the same `wakil source: ...` /
151	`wakil ingest: ...` message conventions `kb-commit` uses elsewhere. That's
152	appropriate when the automatic DAG output is the whole story. Once this
153	workflow continues past the DAG into `entity-enrichment`, `note-routing`,
154	or `note-conformance` — writing or moving files those flags don't know
155	about — skip the CLI's own commit flags and hand the full set of changes to
156	`kb-commit` for one reviewable commit instead of committing the DAG's
157	output separately from what came after it.
158	
159	## Batch ingestion
160	
161	Ingesting many items in one pass — a folder of PDFs, an inbox of captured
162	links — is `source-ingestion`'s test-3-5-before-bulk discipline applied at
163	the orchestration level too: run the full workflow above end-to-end on a
164	handful of items first, inspect the committed result, and only then repeat
165	it across the rest. A classification or routing bug caught on 3 items is a
166	fix; the same bug applied silently across 300 is a rebuild.
167

1	---
2	name: source-ingestion
3	description: Normalize non-native source material (meeting exports, PDFs, voice notes, YouTube videos, scanned documents) into wakil's three CLI-native shapes — transcript, text, or article — with a rich --context string, before handing off to `wakil ingest`. Use whenever raw material doesn't already fit one of those three shapes as-is.
4	skill_api: 1
5	---
6	
7	# source-ingestion
8	
9	`wakil ingest` only knows three shapes of input: a transcript file, a plain
10	text file, and a web article URL. Most of what actually shows up — a PDF
11	email export, a voice memo, a YouTube link, a scanned document, a folder of
12	mixed files — is none of these until someone makes it one. That's this
13	skill's whole job: turn whatever raw material arrived into one of the three
14	CLI-native shapes, with a `--context` string rich enough that the model
15	steps downstream don't have to guess, and then get out of the way.
16	
17	This is deliberately upstream of judgment about what the material *means*.
18	Don't extract claims, don't decide what's worth a note, don't resolve
19	entities here — that's the ingestion DAG's job once your normalized file
20	reaches it.
21	
22	## Where this sits in the pipeline
23	
24	```text
25	raw material (any shape)
26	        │
27	        │  source-ingestion — THIS skill: normalize to transcript/text/article
28	        ▼
29	wakil ingest transcript|text|article    (capture: deterministic, no model)
30	        │
31	        ▼
32	wakil enrich <source-id>                (DAG: extraction → entity resolution → apply)
33	        │
34	        ├─ DAG node 1: transcript, text, or article skill — extraction
35	        │  judgment
36	        └─ DAG node 2: entity-resolve skill — always invoked
37	```
38	
39	`article`/`text`/`transcript`/`entity-resolve` live under `src/wakil/skills/`
40	alongside this 12-skill catalog and are resolved, overridden, and validated
41	the same way (`wakil skills list/which/validate` show them too) — but they're
42	invoked automatically by `wakil enrich`
43	(`src/wakil/app/ingest_service.py`), not part of *this* 12-skill catalog, and
44	this skill does not re-derive their judgment. Once your normalized file is
45	captured, their extraction and entity-resolution judgment takes over; nothing
46	here should anticipate or duplicate it.
47	
48	Deciding *whether* a given piece of raw material needs this
49	pre-normalization step at all, and actually invoking `wakil ingest` /
50	`wakil enrich`, is `ingest-source`'s call. This skill's job ends the moment
51	material exists as a transcript/text/article-shaped file (or a directly
52	fetchable article URL) with a `--context` string ready to hand off.
53	
54	If the material is already fully normalized and you're deciding what to
55	*say* about it — which claims matter, what to quote, how it connects to
56	existing notes — that's `content-synthesis`'s territory, not this skill's.
57	
58	## The three CLI-native shapes, and everything else
59	
60	- **`wakil ingest transcript <file>`** — a meeting or call transcript
61	  (`.txt`, `.md`, `.srt`). Multi-party, dated, attributable to speakers.
62	- **`wakil ingest text <file>`** — a plain text file, pasted note, or
63	  clipping. Solo narration, a fragment, anything that isn't a dialogue
64	  between named parties.
65	- **`wakil ingest article <url>`** — a web article URL, fetched and
66	  extracted directly. Only for content already reachable as a URL.
67	
68	Every one of the three accepts `--context` / `-C`: a few lines about the
69	source (attendees, company, purpose) that feeds directly into the
70	downstream extraction judgment — a transcript's DAG node 1 explicitly uses
71	it to resolve first names and pronouns to full names. Building a strong
72	`--context` string is as much a part of normalization as producing the file
73	itself; a well-shaped transcript with a thin or missing context string
74	still leaves the extraction step guessing.
75	
76	**Anything that isn't already one of these three shapes must be
77	pre-normalized into one before `wakil ingest` runs.** A PDF, a voice memo,
78	a scanned document, a YouTube video — none of these can be handed to
79	`wakil ingest` directly; wakil has no binary or audio/video ingestion path.
80	Extract the material to text (or, for audio/video, to a transcript of what
81	was said), decide honestly whether the result reads as a transcript
82	(multiple speakers, a call or meeting) or as text (a monologue, a document,
83	a clipping), write it to a plain-text file, and compose the `--context`
84	string before invoking `wakil ingest`. See `references/source-types.md` for
85	the per-source-type judgment — what to extract, how to classify it, and
86	where each legacy format's genuine hard-won judgment carries over.
87	
88	## Exact-phrasing preservation
89	
90	When normalizing captures someone's original words — a transcript, a voice
91	note, a quoted passage — use their exact words. Don't paraphrase, don't
92	clean up grammar, don't smooth over hesitations or filler in a spoken
93	transcript. The language is the insight, and normalization is exactly the
94	step where that phrasing is easiest to lose: a transcription pass or a
95	text-extraction tool that "cleans up" the output as a side effect quietly
96	destroys the thing worth capturing. Write the normalized file with the
97	source's own wording intact; let paraphrase happen later, if at all, during
98	synthesis — never during normalization.
99	
100	Back-linking every mention of a person or company that already has a page
101	back to wherever it was mentioned is a related but separate discipline —
102	an unlinked mention is a broken knowledge base. That linking happens
103	downstream, during entity resolution and enrichment, once the normalized
104	file has been captured; this skill's contribution is making sure the
105	`--context` string names the people and companies involved clearly enough
106	that the downstream step can actually find and link them.
107	
108	## Extraction integrity
109	
110	Never trust working memory for a figure, amount, date, or exact phrase
111	that needs to go into the normalized file or its `--context` string.
112	Re-read it from the extracted source at the moment of writing — a PDF's
113	`pdftotext` output, a fetched transcript, an OCR pass — rather than
114	recalling it from earlier in the conversation. This is exactly where batch
115	normalization goes wrong: several PDFs or transcripts get extracted in one
116	session, and a number or name from one bleeds into the write-up of another
117	because it was carried in memory instead of re-read from the file that was
118	actually saved to disk.
119	
120	## Test 3-5 before bulk
121	
122	Before running any bulk normalization — a folder of PDFs, an email export
123	with dozens of messages, a batch of voice memos — normalize and ingest a
124	small sample (3-5 items) first and inspect the resulting captures by hand
125	before processing the rest. A bug in the extraction or classification logic
126	that corrupts 3 files is a quick fix; the same bug silently applied across
127	300 is a rebuild. Wakil's own `wakil schema migrate` embodies this
128	discipline structurally — `schema_migrate_service.py` only ever proposes a
129	migration and diffs it before anything is rewritten, and re-verifies each
130	file is unchanged since planning before it touches disk. Bulk normalization
131	has no equivalent built-in safety net, so apply the same discipline by
132	hand: sample, inspect, then proceed.
133	
134	## Handing off
135	
136	Once material is normalized, hand off in order:
137	
138	- [ ] Step 1: Normalize the material into one of the three CLI-native
139	      shapes (`transcript`/`text`/`article`) with a rich `--context` string,
140	      as described above.
141	- [ ] Step 2: Run `wakil ingest transcript|text|article` with the
142	      `--context` string you built. That capture step is deterministic — no
143	      model runs, nothing is interpreted — so a thin context string here is
144	      a problem you can't fix later by hoping the extraction step
145	      compensates.
146	- [ ] Step 3: Let `wakil enrich <source-id>` run the extraction and
147	      entity-resolution DAG automatically; you do not need to (and should
148	      not) pre-decide what the material means or which entities it
149	      touches.
150	- [ ] Step 4: Hand off further judgment as needed. If you're deciding
151	      whether normalization was even the right call, or orchestrating the
152	      ingest/enrich sequence itself (branches, commits, PRs), that's
153	      `ingest-source`'s territory. If the resulting note needs a home
154	      beyond what `wakil enrich` proposes, or needs merging into a note
155	      that already exists, that's `note-routing` and `note-revision`,
156	      respectively — not this skill.
157

1	# Per-source-type normalization judgment
2	
3	Dispatch table for `source-ingestion`. Each section covers one non-native
4	source shape: what genuine judgment from prior experience carries over,
5	what to extract, and which of wakil's three CLI-native shapes
6	(`transcript` / `text` / `article`) the result becomes. None of this
7	decides what the material *means* — that's the ingestion DAG's job once
8	`wakil ingest` runs.
9	
10	## Contents
11	
12	- [Meeting transcripts](#meeting-transcripts-from-exports-pdfs-or-raw-capture-files)
13	- [PDFs](#pdfs-documents-contracts-email-thread-exports)
14	- [Voice notes](#voice-notes)
15	- [YouTube videos](#youtube-videos)
16	- [OCR / scanned documents](#ocr--scanned-documents)
17	- [Deferred: media ingest and archive crawling](#deferred-media-ingest-and-archive-crawling)
18	
19	## Meeting transcripts (from exports, PDFs, or raw capture files)
20	
21	Destination shape: `wakil ingest transcript`.
22	
23	- **Attendee identification belongs in `--context`, not in manual page
24	  creation.** `wakil enrich`'s entity-resolution DAG step (the
25	  `entity-resolve` skill) is always invoked and will create or update
26	  attendee pages itself — don't do that by hand here. What normalization
27	  contributes is making sure the extraction step doesn't have to guess: list
28	  attendees with full names, roles, and company in the `--context` string.
29	  The `transcript` skill explicitly uses this context to resolve first names
30	  and pronouns to full names — a transcript normalized without it forces the
31	  extraction step to guess who "Jane" or "he" refers to.
32	- **Verify proper-noun spelling before it goes into the context string or
33	  the file.** Auto-generated transcripts and hand-typed filenames
34	  frequently misspell names and company names. Cross-check against an
35	  authoritative source when one is available (an email thread, the
36	  company's own site, a press release or LinkedIn URL) before it becomes
37	  the spelling that gets propagated into an entity's canonical name
38	  downstream — a typo caught here is a five-second fix; a typo that
39	  becomes a page name is a rename later.
40	- **Meeting date is not capture date.** wakil's own `source` schema
41	  distinguishes them for transcript-origin sources: `captured` (when the
42	  file was captured) and `meeting_date` (when the meeting actually
43	  happened) are separate fields (`src/wakil/schema/entities/source.yaml`,
44	  `origins.transcript`). A filename or file-system timestamp is a capture
45	  artifact, not evidence of when the meeting occurred — if the transcript
46	  content or surrounding context establishes a different date, put the
47	  real meeting date in `--context` and let it flow into `meeting_date`
48	  rather than trusting the filename.
49	- **Prep-doc reconciliation is real, workspace-owned judgment.** If the
50	  workspace keeps a prep note ahead of meetings (its own convention, not a
51	  wakil field), and one exists for this meeting, read it before
52	  normalizing: pull its planned questions and flagged topics into the
53	  `--context` string so the extraction step can note what got resolved
54	  and what's still open, and plan to cross-link the meeting note back to
55	  the prep note once both exist. Follow whatever the workspace's own
56	  `RESOLVER.md`/`SCHEMA.md` say a prep note looks like — don't invent a
57	  frontmatter shape for it.
58	- **A header-only or partial transcript is a valid capture, not an
59	  error.** Normalize and ingest what exists, note in `--context` that the
60	  capture is partial, and re-run `wakil ingest`/`wakil enrich` once the
61	  full transcript is available rather than waiting to ingest anything.
62	- **Flag suspicious numeric claims rather than silently normalizing
63	  them.** Conversational settings are where equity percentages get
64	  confused with basis points, round sizes get misquoted, and headcounts
65	  get rounded into "hired" when the source actually meant "interviewed."
66	  When something reads as an obvious unit or magnitude error, note both
67	  the verbatim claim and the likely correction in `--context` — don't
68	  quietly fix it and don't quietly drop it.
69	
70	## PDFs (documents, contracts, email thread exports)
71	
72	Destination shape: `wakil ingest text` (or `transcript`, if the PDF is
73	itself a meeting-transcript export — see above).
74	
75	- **Extract text before wakil ever sees the file.** wakil has no binary
76	  ingestion path — a `.pdf` path handed to `wakil ingest` is not something
77	  it can parse. Extract to plain text first (a layout-preserving mode when
78	  the document has tables or columns matters — a naive extraction can
79	  scramble reading order), and review the extracted text before writing it
80	  to the file `wakil ingest` will read.
81	- **Classify before normalizing.** A PDF might be an email thread, a
82	  meeting transcript export, a contract, a resume, or a clipped article.
83	  The classification decides the destination shape and which entities the
84	  `--context` string should call out — an email thread's participants are
85	  its context in the same way a meeting's attendees are.
86	- **De-duplicate quoted and forwarded content in email exports.** Email
87	  thread PDFs routinely contain the same earlier message quoted or
88	  forwarded multiple times as the thread grows. Strip the duplication
89	  before writing the normalized file — otherwise the same claim gets
90	  captured (and later extracted) several times over, and a downstream
91	  read overweights it.
92	- **Never pass the PDF path itself onward.** Not to `wakil ingest`, not
93	  embedded as a reference in the normalized text file in place of its
94	  content. The extracted text is the source of truth `wakil ingest`
95	  captures; the original PDF is provenance, not input.
96	
97	## Voice notes
98	
99	Destination shape: almost always `wakil ingest text` — a voice note is
100	solo narration, not a dialogue between named parties, so it rarely
101	qualifies as a `transcript`. Use `transcript` only if the recording is
102	itself a multi-party call.
103	
104	- **Transcribe verbatim.** This is the sharpest case of exact-phrasing
105	  preservation: hesitations, filler words, unfinished sentences, and rough
106	  phrasing are exactly what makes a voice note worth capturing over a
107	  cleaned-up written note. Don't let a transcription tool's "clean mode"
108	  smooth any of it out.
109	- **Don't pre-decide the subject-matter classification here.** Whether
110	  this note is best understood as a new idea, a reflection, an update
111	  about a person, or something else is a routing/synthesis judgment made
112	  after capture — by `note-routing` once a note is proposed — not
113	  something to resolve while normalizing the raw transcript. What
114	  normalization contributes instead: a `--context` string naming the
115	  channel, date, and — when the note is clearly about a specific person or
116	  company — who or what it concerns, so the downstream steps have enough
117	  to work with.
118	
119	## YouTube videos
120	
121	Destination shape: `wakil ingest text` for a monologue or single-narrator
122	video; `wakil ingest transcript` if the video is substantially an
123	interview or multi-party conversation.
124	
125	- **Fetch the transcript, don't summarize the video description.** A
126	  video's real content is its transcript (captions or an automated
127	  transcription), not its title or blurb.
128	- **If transcripts are disabled or unavailable, say so rather than
129	  fabricating a summary from the title and description.** A missing
130	  transcript is a dead end for this skill, not something to paper over
131	  with a guess at what the video probably covers.
132	- **Put the video title, channel/speaker, and URL in `--context`.** That's
133	  the equivalent of a transcript's attendee list — it's what lets the
134	  downstream extraction step attribute claims correctly.
135	- **Chunking a very long video's transcript for readability is a capture
136	  concern, not a synthesis one; how much of a long transcript is worth
137	  deep synthesis is `content-synthesis`'s long-document strategy, not
138	  this skill's.** Normalize the whole fetched transcript into the file;
139	  don't pre-trim it down to what seems most relevant.
140	
141	## OCR / scanned documents
142	
143	Destination shape: `wakil ingest text`.
144	
145	- **Try direct text extraction first.** Most PDFs and scanned exports
146	  that look "scanned" still carry an embedded text layer; a plain
147	  extraction pass is faster and more faithful than OCR whenever it works.
148	- **Fall back to OCR only when direct extraction is empty or clearly
149	  garbled**, not as a default first step — OCR is slower, and its output
150	  needs the same review-before-writing discipline as any other
151	  extraction.
152	- **When OCR-ing a batch of scanned pages or documents, check a few pages'
153	  output quality before committing to the full batch.** This is the
154	  test-3-5-before-bulk discipline applied specifically to OCR: a
155	  systematic misread (a font OCR handles badly, a skewed scan) shows up
156	  in the first few pages just as reliably as in the three-hundredth, and
157	  catching it early avoids reprocessing everything.
158

160

162	on but are **not yet automated here**. Both are real needs — a
163	video/audio/screenshot/repo ingestion pipeline, and a tool for crawling

167	ordinary instances of the source types above: normalize each one by hand
168	into a `text`/`article`/`transcript` shape plus a rich `--context`
169	string, and use `wakil ingest` directly, one item at a time.

# Audit: does the skill catalog capture meeting-ingestion's nuance?

## Context

While improving `wakil ingest transcript`'s `.whisper` support this session, I
proposed adding two guidance bullets to `skills/transcript/SKILL.md` to cover
stutter-repair/title-synthesis polish. The user pushed back: that skill (and
`article`/`text` alongside it) reads as far thinner than
`.hermes/skills/meeting-ingestion/SKILL.md` (260+ lines encoding real,
hard-won judgment from a mature system), and asked directly whether a "small"
change could actually capture that nuance.

The honest answer required auditing the *whole* current skill catalog against
meeting-ingestion line-by-line, not just the one file I'd been looking at —
because another agent has been concurrently landing a skill-catalog refactor
throughout this session (`git log`: `13ef03e`, `cab8f23`, PR #12), and its
output changes the answer substantially.

## What the audit found

**Most of the nuance is already ported — not into `skills/transcript/SKILL.md`,
but into `skills/source-ingestion/references/source-types.md`** (written this
session, per file mtimes). Line-by-line against meeting-ingestion:

| meeting-ingestion nugget | Status |
|---|---|
| Meeting date ≠ capture date | ✅ ported, `source-types.md`, tied to wakil's actual `source.yaml` schema fields |
| Verify entity spelling before slugging | ✅ ported, `source-types.md` |
| Numeric-claim sanity check (bps, ARR, headcount) | ✅ ported near-verbatim, `source-types.md` |
| Header-only/stub transcript is valid, not an error | ✅ ported, `source-types.md` |
| Prep-doc reconciliation | ✅ ported as "workspace-owned judgment," `source-types.md` |
| Preserve verbatim language for decisive exchanges | ✅ covered — `transcript/SKILL.md` + `content-synthesis`'s "Verbatim quotes over paraphrase" |
| Anchor on resolution, not the first option raised | ✅ covered, `transcript/SKILL.md` |
| Re-read source rather than trust working memory | ✅ generalized well — "Extraction integrity" appears in `content-synthesis`, `note-revision`, `source-ingestion` |
| Mandatory attendee/entity page creation + back-links | ✅ covered — by wakil's always-invoked entity-resolution DAG step + `entity-enrichment`, explicitly cross-referenced in `source-types.md` |
| gbrain CLI calls, bd/kanban task-tracking, `check-backlinks`, `gog` email retrieval | ❌ correctly **not** ported — this is exactly the tool-coupling `docs/skill-refactor.md` calls out as "a key source of the rot" |
| **Joint-pronoun structural-accountability signal** ("we hold them responsible" implies shared accountability) | ❌ genuine gap, not ported anywhere |
| **Two-part output format** (status line + prioritized red/yellow/green "Action Items for You") | ❌ genuine gap, not ported anywhere |

So: my original "small change" instinct was wrong for the wrong reason last
turn (I hadn't found `source-types.md` yet and thought almost everything was
missing), but the corrected conclusion is still that only a **small, now
precisely-scoped** change remains — because the concurrent refactor already
did the heavy lifting, in the architecturally correct place.

**Also found, unrelated to the nuance question but a direct regression from
my own work this session:** `ingest-source/SKILL.md`'s dispatch table and
`source-ingestion/SKILL.md`'s "three CLI-native shapes" list both still say
`.whisper` needs `source-ingestion` normalization first. That's now stale —
`wakil ingest transcript` parses `.whisper` natively as of this session's
earlier change (`ingest_service.py`'s `parse_whisper_transcript`). Left
unfixed, an agent following these skills would mis-route already-native
`.whisper` files through an unnecessary normalization step.

## Recommended plan

Three small, independent edits — no new skills, no restructuring:

1. **`src/wakil/skills/transcript/SKILL.md`** — add one bullet on the
   joint-pronoun signal: language like "we hold them responsible" / "you, me,
   we" / "between us" is a structural signal that both parties share
   accountability, not rhetorical filler; a memory or note that puts the
   burden on only one party when the transcript used joint-pronoun language is
   worth a second look. This is transcript-specific interpretation judgment
   (not a normalization concern), so it belongs here, not in
   `source-types.md`.

2. **`src/wakil/skills/ingest-source/SKILL.md`** — add a short "Reporting
   back" section (or extend an existing step) describing a two-part response
   after a meeting/call ingest that drove or will drive a user decision:  a
   one-line status summary, plus — only when the source drove or will drive a
   downstream user action — a prioritized action-items list (this-week /
   before-next-milestone / informational), distinguishing what the user owes
   from what they're waiting on the counterparty for. Skip the second part for
   purely informational sources. This is orchestration-level "how to hand
   results back," matching `ingest-source`'s existing role as the top-level
   workflow skill, not a per-source-type extraction concern.

3. **Mechanical fix**: update the two stale CLI-native-shape references —
   `ingest-source/SKILL.md`'s dispatch table row for transcripts (add
   `.whisper`) and `source-ingestion/SKILL.md`'s "three CLI-native shapes"
   list (note that `.whisper` is now natively handled by `wakil ingest
   transcript`, no `source-ingestion` pre-normalization needed). Small text
   edits, no behavior change — just correcting now-stale guidance so an agent
   reading these skills doesn't route `.whisper` files through an unnecessary
   manual normalization step.

**Explicitly not doing:** rewriting `article`/`text`/`transcript` to be as
long as `meeting-ingestion/SKILL.md`. Their brevity is now understood to be
intentional given the catalog's layering — `source-ingestion` owns
per-format normalization judgment, `content-synthesis`/`entity-enrichment`/
`note-revision` own cross-cutting synthesis judgment, and `transcript`/`text`/
`article` stay narrow, DAG-node-scoped extraction prompts by design
(`content-synthesis/SKILL.md`'s own text: "those skills are authoritative...
don't re-derive their judgment here"). Padding them out would duplicate
guidance that already has a correct, more general home elsewhere in the
catalog — the opposite of what the refactor is for.

## Verification

- `uv run wakil -w <sandbox-kb> skills validate` after each edit — confirms
  frontmatter/metadata still valid post-edit.
- Re-read the edited files against the meeting-ingestion checklist above to
  confirm the two identified gaps are actually closed and nothing new was
  introduced that duplicates `source-types.md`'s existing coverage.
- No test suite coverage needed — these are prose-only skill files with no
  Python behavior; `uv run pytest tests/unit/test_skills_resolver.py` (once
  the concurrent refactor's own unrelated failures there are resolved) is the
  right smoke check that resolution still finds them.

1	---
2	name: ingest-source
3	description: Orchestrate the end-to-end path from raw external material to a committed, linked, conformant knowledge-base note — normalize, capture, enrich, resolve entities, route, and conform — resuming by source id on failure. Use whenever asked to ingest, capture, or process external material into the knowledge base.
4	skill_api: 1
5	---
6	
7	# ingest-source
8	
9	This is the top-level, user-facing workflow. It does not do its own content
10	judgment — it decides which of the six focused skills below apply to the
11	material in front of it, in what order, and gets out of the way once each
12	has done its job. If you catch yourself deciding what a note should say,
13	which entity a mention resolves to, or where a file belongs, stop — that
14	judgment belongs to `content-synthesis`, `entity-resolution`, or
15	`note-routing` respectively, not to this skill.
16	
17	## The two-command backbone
18	
19	For the three shapes `wakil` ingests natively, the whole pipeline is two
20	commands:
21	
22	```text
23	wakil ingest {transcript,text,article}     step 1: capture (deterministic, no model)
24	wakil enrich <source-id>                   step 2: analyze and link (model-driven DAG)
25	```
26	
27	`wakil ingest` writes the raw material under `sources/` and records a
28	`Source` row, nothing more — no interpretation happens at this step.
29	`wakil enrich <source-id>` then runs a fixed, code-sequenced DAG
30	(`src/wakil/app/ingest_service.py`, `prepare_enrichment`):
31	
32	1. **DAG node 1 — extraction.** Runs the CLI-native judgment from the
33	   `transcript`/`text`/`article` skill (this is exactly what
34	   `content-synthesis` describes as already handled for native source
35	   types) and produces a proposed primary note.
36	2. **DAG node 2 — entity resolution.** Always invoked, never optional.
37	   Runs the `entity-resolve` skill (the same judgment `entity-resolution`
38	   documents) and, for every entity it decides to create, writes a
39	   schema-routed stub page via `schema.directory` — the deterministic slice
40	   of what `note-routing` calls "entity types are code-owned."
41	3. **Validation gate.** `validate_proposal()` checks every proposed file
42	   carries schema-valid frontmatter for its `type:` and hard-stops on an
43	   unrecognized type or a duplicate path — a partial, mechanical slice of
44	   what `note-conformance` checks in full.
45	
46	Then one preview, one confirm, one apply. Nothing is written before you
47	confirm; nothing partial is left behind if you decline.
48	
49	## Where the automatic DAG stops — and why this skill exists beyond it
50	
51	The DAG above gives you a schema-valid primary note plus schema-valid entity
52	stubs. It does **not**:
53	
54	- write texture into a stub's State (Compiled Truth), decide which of the
55	  source's *other* mentions earn a back-link, or add Timeline entries beyond what
56	  extraction directly proposed — that's `entity-enrichment`'s job, per its
57	  own description of exactly this gap;
58	- route the primary note through the workspace's `RESOLVER.md` — the
59	  extraction skill picks the proposed note's path itself, so anything that
60	  needs workspace-specific subject-matter placement beyond what the
61	  extraction skill already decided is `note-routing`'s job;
62	- run the full no-slop prose bar, three-way slug consistency, or link-format
63	  audit — only frontmatter schema validity is checked automatically; the
64	  rest is `note-conformance`'s job.
65	
66	So: for material where the automatic stub-and-scaffold output is genuinely
67	sufficient (a minor mention, a low-stakes capture), `wakil enrich` alone may
68	be enough. For anything that matters — a page worth real texture, a note
69	whose placement isn't obvious from the extraction skill's own guess, a
70	result you're about to commit — continue the workflow by hand through
71	`entity-enrichment` → `note-routing` → `note-conformance` before handing the
72	result to `kb-commit`. Use judgment on how far to go; don't assume the DAG's
73	automatic output is the finished product just because it applied cleanly.
74	
75	## Dispatch: does the material need normalizing first?
76	
77	| Material | Path |
78	|---|---|
79	| Meeting/call transcript file (`.txt`, `.md`, `.srt`) | CLI-native — `wakil ingest transcript` directly |
80	| Plain text, pasted note, clipping | CLI-native — `wakil ingest text` directly |
81	| Web article URL | CLI-native — `wakil ingest article` directly |
82	| PDF, voice note, YouTube video, scanned/OCR document, or anything else not already one of the three shapes above | Normalize first via `source-ingestion`, then continue through the same two-command backbone |
83	
84	`source-ingestion` owns all of the per-source-type judgment for the
85	normalize-first column — what to extract, how to classify the result as
86	`transcript` vs. `text`, and how to build a `--context` string rich enough
87	for DAG node 1 to use. Don't re-derive that judgment here; hand the
88	material off and resume once it's normalized.
89	
90	## Full workflow
91	
92	```text
93	source-ingestion            (only when normalization is needed — see dispatch table)
94	        ↓
95	wakil ingest {shape}         capture: writes sources/*, deterministic
96	        ↓
97	wakil enrich <source-id>     DAG: content-synthesis (native judgment)
98	        ↓                         + entity-resolution + schema-valid stubs
99	entity-enrichment            texture, back-links, Timeline beyond the DAG's proposal
100	        ↓
101	note-routing                 placement for anything not already schema-routed
102	        ↓
103	note-conformance             full schema/slug/link/prose audit
104	        ↓
105	kb-commit                    reviewable diff, commit
106	```
107	
108	Each stage's output is distinct, and that separation is the point — a
109	retry at any stage doesn't repeat the stages before it:
110	
111	1. **`source-ingestion`** (conditional) → a normalized transcript/text file
112	   plus a `--context` string, ready for `wakil ingest`.
113	2. **`wakil ingest`** → the raw source note under `sources/`, recorded with
114	   a source id.
115	3. **`wakil enrich`** → a proposed primary note plus schema-valid entity
116	   stubs, previewed and applied together.
117	4. **`entity-enrichment`** → back-links, Compiled Truth texture, and
118	   Timeline entries the DAG didn't generate on its own.
119	5. **`note-routing`** → a destination directory and filename for anything
120	   the DAG's own extraction-skill guess didn't already settle.
121	6. **`note-conformance`** → a note that's schema-valid, consistently
122	   slugged, cleanly linked, and free of slop — ready to commit.
123	7. **`kb-commit`** → the actual commit, with a message and diff the user
124	   can review.
125	
126	## Resuming a failed or interrupted run
127	
128	Track progress by **source id**, not by re-running earlier stages:
129	
130	- Capture is idempotent by content hash — re-running `wakil ingest` on
131	  material already captured reports the existing source id and writes
132	  nothing new. It is safe to re-run, but it does not advance a stalled
133	  pipeline; resume with `wakil enrich <source-id>` instead.
134	- If capture succeeded but `wakil enrich` failed, was declined at the
135	  confirmation prompt, or `validate_proposal()` blocked it on a schema
136	  issue — fix the underlying cause (an unrecognized entity type, a
137	  workspace schema gap) and re-run `wakil enrich <source-id>`. Don't
138	  re-capture; the source already exists.
139	- To re-analyze a source that already completed enrichment (new
140	  information surfaced, the first pass was thin), re-run
141	  `wakil enrich <source-id> --force`.
142	- If enrichment applied but the manual stages (`entity-enrichment`,
143	  `note-routing`, `note-conformance`) haven't run yet, pick up from
144	  whichever of those is next — each is safe to run on the DAG's output
145	  independent of how capture or enrichment went.
146	
147	## Committing
148	
149	`wakil ingest`/`wakil enrich` can commit their own output directly via
150	`--commit`/`--branch`/`--pr`, using the same `wakil source: ...` /
151	`wakil ingest: ...` message conventions `kb-commit` uses elsewhere. That's
152	appropriate when the automatic DAG output is the whole story. Once this
153	workflow continues past the DAG into `entity-enrichment`, `note-routing`,
154	or `note-conformance` — writing or moving files those flags don't know
155	about — skip the CLI's own commit flags and hand the full set of changes to
156	`kb-commit` for one reviewable commit instead of committing the DAG's
157	output separately from what came after it.
158	
159	## Batch ingestion
160	
161	Ingesting many items in one pass — a folder of PDFs, an inbox of captured
162	links — is `source-ingestion`'s test-3-5-before-bulk discipline applied at
163	the orchestration level too: run the full workflow above end-to-end on a
164	handful of items first, inspect the committed result, and only then repeat
165	it across the rest. A classification or routing bug caught on 3 items is a
166	fix; the same bug applied silently across 300 is a rebuild.

14	_FTS_TABLES = [
15	    ("notes_fts", "notes", ["title", "path", "frontmatter_json"]),
16	    ("memories_fts", "memories", ["content", "summary"]),
17	    ("sources_fts", "sources", ["title", "origin", "author"]),

21	def _fts_statements() -> list[str]:
22	    statements = []
23	    for fts, table, columns in _FTS_TABLES:
24	        cols = ", ".join(columns)

29	            f"{cols}, content='{table}', content_rowid='id')",
30	            f"CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS {table}_fts_insert AFTER INSERT ON {table} BEGIN "
31	            f"INSERT INTO {fts}(rowid, {cols}) VALUES (new.id, {new_vals}); END",
32	            f"CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS {table}_fts_delete AFTER DELETE ON {table} BEGIN "

34	            f"CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS {table}_fts_update AFTER UPDATE ON {table} BEGIN "
35	            f"INSERT INTO {fts}({fts}, rowid, {cols}) VALUES ('delete', old.id, {old_vals}); "
36	            f"INSERT INTO {fts}(rowid, {cols}) VALUES (new.id, {new_vals}); END",

All three real bugs traced back to one thing: **entity-resolution's only view of existing pages was a generic relevance search** (`related_query = title + context + text[:300]`, top 5 results). I reproduced your exact run and found why that search failed here:

- QMD returned a flat `"score": 0.88` on *every* result for a "Mosaic" query — confirmed by running the raw `qmd` CLI directly, not a wakil parsing bug. QMD isn't grading relevance at all in this mode, so its result order is close to arbitrary (`people/manasa-grandhi.md` ranked above `companies/mosaic-private-markets.md` and `people/ian-gutwinski.md`, which didn't make the top 5 at all).
- FTS5 only indexes `title`/`path`/`frontmatter_json` for notes, and with no stopword filtering, your ~80-token blended query let content-rich duplicate meeting notes (matching many of the incidental words) outrank a sparse entity stub whose title is just "Mosaic."

So entity-resolution never saw `companies/mosaic-private-markets.md` or `people/ian-gutwinski.md` in its prompt — it couldn't match what it was never shown. (I'm not touching QMD's scoring itself — that's a deeper, separate question your own `TODO.md` already flags as unverified against a real install; wrong to guess-fix blind.)

## What I fixed

1. **New deterministic name lookup** (`_candidate_entity_notes` in `ingest_service.py`) — pulls proper-noun phrases from the source text/context and does a direct title match against notes under identity/hybrid-category entity directories (`people/`, `companies/`, `concepts/`, etc.), independent of QMD/FTS ranking. Supplements the existing relevance search rather than replacing it.
2. **Missing source-link field** — extraction now gets the raw *capture's* path (`sources/transcripts/...md`) instead of the pre-capture origin (which could be a `.whisper` file the model can't cite), and `transcript`/`article`/`text` skills now instruct filling a schema-defined back-link field with it.

Re-running `enrich 1 --force` now resolves **Ian Gutwinski → `people/ian-gutwinski.md` (0.97)**, **Mosaic → `companies/mosaic-private-markets.md` (0.90)** (plus Riviera Partners and Radical Ventures, unprompted), and the proposed note carries `transcript: sources/transcripts/2026-07-16-mosaic-eleni-karahalios.md`. Nothing was written — I declined the confirm prompt.

## Not bugs, for the record

- **`drafts/` routing**: correct, intentional collision-avoidance — `meetings/2026/2026-07-16-mosaic-eleni-karahalios-backchannel.md` already exists (from your earlier legacy-skill comparison run), and wakil never overwrites. content.text:
I did a line-by-line diff of both outputs against `schema.md`, and found the gap is bigger — and more fixable — than the four bugs from last turn. There's one root cause behind most of it.

## The headline finding: `SCHEMA.md` is silently truncated before the part wakil needs most

`load_workspace_guides()` caps every guide file at `GUIDE_MAX_CHARS = 4_000` (`ingest_service.py:64,880`) with a blind slice — no warning, no visibility. This KB's `schema.md` is **6,538 chars**, and the `### meeting` frontmatter template — the one defining `source`, `attendees`, `company`, `project`, `decisions`, `action-items`, `transcript` — starts at **char 4,191**. The model never sees it. It only ever sees section 1 (naming) and section 2, which is explicitly titled *"The Page Standard (compiled truth + timeline)"* and opens with *"Every important entity page has two parts…"* That's the only page-shape guidance available, so:

- **The wakil draft uses the entity-page shape (Compiled Truth + Timeline) for a meeting**, which `schema.md` itself scopes to entity pages, not documents. The legacy output uses a purpose-built event shape — `## Summary` / `## Key Decisions` / `## Action Items` / `## Discussion Notes` — that wakil's model was never shown and has no other way to learn.
- **Frontmatter is missing `source`, `project`, `decisions`, `action-items`, `transcript`** (the last one I already fixed to populate — but the model still never saw the field *name* to know to look for it from schema.md itself, it just happened to get filled via the skill-prose change). None of this is a validation bug — wakil's own `meeting.yaml` correctly marks these `required: false`, so `validate_proposal()` passed a technically-valid but much thinner note.
- **The `confidence: medium` field wakil invented** isn't fabricated — it's real, from `schema.md` §3 ("`confidence: low|medium|high` in frontmatter for synthesized pages") — which the model *did* see (it's before the cutoff), while never seeing §3's actual citation mechanism it's paired with.

This one constant is the highest-leverage fix available — it's a single number, and it's actively discarding the part of this KB's schema the model needs most. `RESOLVER.md` is 3,096 chars — safe today, but the same cliff as this KB grows.

## Consequences, once you look past the truncation

- **Per-fact citations are absent.** `schema.md` §3 documents an inline provenance convention (`(observed)`, `(reported: <source>)`) — technically past the cutoff too, but even independent of that, nothing in `content-synthesis`/`transcript` instructs checking for a citation convention at all. The legacy output cites *every* bullet (`[Source: Meeting "...", 2026-07-16]` — its own format, not even schema.md's). Wakil's Compiled Truth has zero inline attribution.
- **Self-entity linking is broken.** `people/edward-bridges.md` exists (a real self-page, `name: Edward Bridges`) — confirmed by my earlier fix's own name-lookup, which *would* surface it as a candidate. Entity-resolution still resolved "Edward Bridges" as `skip` (0.90 confidence). `entity-resolve/SKILL.md` has no self-entity guidance at all, unlike the legacy skill's explicit carve-out ("unless the attendee is the user/self *and no self-page convention exists*"). Since this KB clearly has that convention, wakil should be linking it and isn't.
- **Thoroughness judgment, not just field-presence.** Even with the schema visible, nothing pushes the model to actually *fill* optional-but-supported fields when the source clearly has them (this transcript has explicit next steps and an explicit "no decisions made" outcome — both cleanly mappable to `decisions: []` / `action-items: [...]`). `note-conformance` checks shape/schema-validity, not content-completeness against what the source actually supports.

## Recommended fixes, roughly by leverage

1. **Raise (or remove) `GUIDE_MAX_CHARS`, and stop truncating silently.** At minimum bump it well past any realistic `schema.md`+`RESOLVER.md` size; better, warn (in the preview) when a guide is truncated rather than quietly slicing. This alone likely fixes the frontmatter-completeness and page-shape-default problems for this KB.
2. **Give `content-synthesis`/`transcript` a sensible default document-page shape** (Summary/Decisions/Action-Items/Discussion, roughly) for document-category notes, used only when the workspace's own `SCHEMA.md` doesn't specify one — so a truncation or a thin `schema.md` doesn't silently fall back to the entity-page shape for the wrong category of note.
3. **Teach `entity-resolve` about self-pages**: if a candidate entity matches the workspace's own "self" convention (a person page for the user), resolve it like any other attendee rather than defaulting to skip.
4. **Point `content-synthesis`/`transcript` at `schema.md` §3's citation convention explicitly** — "if the workspace defines an inline provenance format, use it" is a one-line addition once the truncation stops hiding it.

Want me to implement these, starting with #1 (the constant) since it's the one-line fix with the most reach, or would you rather look at the tradeoffs first (e.g., how large a guide cap is safe to send in every prompt)?

# Shift field-shape authority to wakil's built-in schema; shrink schema.md/RESOLVER.md to genuinely-KB-specific prose

## Context

The prior critical-analysis pass found that `wakil enrich`'s frontmatter/page-shape
gaps versus the legacy skill trace mostly to one thing: `load_workspace_guides()`
caps every guide file at `GUIDE_MAX_CHARS = 4_000` and silently slices — this KB's
`schema.md` is 6,538 chars, and the `### meeting` template (the fields the model
most needed) starts at char 4,191, past the cutoff. A background agent then
confirmed a related fact: `validate_proposal()` **already** validates only against
wakil's own `src/wakil/schema/entities/*.yaml`, never against `schema.md` — the
prose schema is *already* redundant with code for validation purposes, just not
yet for the *extraction prompt*, which still depends on schema.md's raw text to
tell the model what fields to fill in.

The user's proposed shift: stop treating `schema.md` as a second, hand-maintained
copy of field shape (a duplication/drift risk `docs/skill-refactor.md` already
names as a rot source), make wakil's built-in entity schema the sole authority for
field shape and validation, and shrink `schema.md` down to prose that genuinely
doesn't reduce to a schema — naming philosophy, page-shape convention, citation
format. Same question extended to `RESOLVER.md`: fold in the parts that aren't
entity-type routing (already code-owned per `note-routing/SKILL.md`'s own stated
split) into wakil as sensible defaults, leaving only genuinely KB-specific
judgment calls in the workspace file.

Reading both files in full surfaced a useful, unplanned data point: this KB's own
`zz-templates/` has no meeting template at all, and its `transcript-template.md`
doesn't even match `schema.md`'s own `### source` block. There is no single
existing canonical "meeting body shape" anywhere in this KB to preserve — the
legacy skill's Summary/Decisions/Action-Items/Discussion-Notes structure is
undocumented tribal knowledge, informally living in one skill file. That
strengthens the case for wakil establishing its own clean, reasoned default rather
than trying to excavate a "correct" answer that doesn't consistently exist.

## What's already true (no change needed)

- `validate_proposal()` and entity stub creation (`_build_stub_entities`) already
  key entirely off `load_entity_schemas()` (`src/wakil/schema/entities/*.yaml`) —
  zero dependency on `schema.md`.
- `note-routing/SKILL.md` already implements exactly this split for *routing*:
  "entity types are code-owned" (`schema.directory`) vs. "everything else is
  workspace-owned, via RESOLVER.md." The user's proposal extends an
  already-proven pattern from routing to shaping, not a new idea.
- `note-conformance/SKILL.md` already duplicates `RESOLVER.md`'s entire
  "Linking" section (absolute-path-only wikilinks) almost verbatim — that section
  of `RESOLVER.md` is pure redundancy today and can simply be deleted from it,
  no wakil change needed.
- Of `RESOLVER.md`'s 10-item decision order, items 2–3 and 5–9 (person, company,
  project, concept, idea, organization, journal) are *already* code-owned via
  `schema.directory` — confirmed each has a `directory:` in
  `src/wakil/schema/entities/*.yaml`. What's genuinely irreducible: the
  concept-vs-project judgment heuristic, the meetings/ (synthesized) vs. sources/
  (raw) split, sensitive-content flagging, and the archive/inbox fallback.

## Recommended approach — three parts, same session

### A. Give extraction the parsed entity schema directly (the core fix)

`build_extraction_prompt` (`src/wakil/llm/prompts.py`) currently receives only
free-text `guides` (schema.md/RESOLVER.md, truncated, unstructured). Unlike
`build_resolution_prompt`, which already takes `entity_types: dict[str,
EntitySchema]` and renders it deterministically, extraction has no structured
view of field shape at all — which is *why* the meeting note came out missing
`source`/`project`/`decisions`/`action-items`: the model was inferring shape from
whatever schema.md prose survived truncation, not from wakil's own schema.

Change `_run_extraction`/`prepare_enrichment` (`ingest_service.py`) to pass
`load_entity_schemas()` through to `build_extraction_prompt`, and render the
relevant type's full field list (name, required/optional, kind) the same way
`_render_related`/the resolution prompt already render structured data — no
truncation risk, since it's rendering parsed fields, not slicing a file. This is
the change that actually fixes frontmatter completeness, independent of anything
schema.md says or how long it is.

### B. Shrink `schema.md` to prose-only; give wakil sensible built-in defaults for it

Once field shape is code-owned, `schema.md`'s job narrows to what doesn't reduce
to YAML: naming conventions (§1), the page-shape convention (§2 — correctly
scoped to *entity* pages, not documents), the citation convention (§3), wikilink
preference (§5). Two things happen together, not sequentially:

1. **This KB's `schema.md` shrinks** to just those sections (KB-owner edit, not a
   wakil change — flagging so it's not lost, but out of scope for this repo).
2. **Wakil's own skills gain sensible defaults** for the same concerns, so a
   workspace with a minimal or absent `schema.md` still behaves well, and a
   present-but-truncated one degrades gracefully instead of losing the *only*
   page-shape guidance the model had:
   - `note-conformance/SKILL.md` gains a default page-shape-by-category rule:
     identity-category → Compiled Truth/Timeline (already implicit in how
     `entity-enrichment`/`note-revision` talk about State+Timeline); document
     category → a Summary/Key-Decisions/Action-Items/Discussion-Notes-style
     default, used when the workspace doesn't specify otherwise.
   - `transcript`/`article`/`text` skills gain a default inline-citation
     instruction (cite claims to their source), overridden by the workspace's
     own format when `schema.md` defines one.
   `schema.md`, still read as today, continues to override these defaults where
   it says something specific — same relationship as now, just far smaller and
   low-stakes if it's ever truncated again, because the part that used to break
   (field shape) no longer depends on it at all.

### C. Fold RESOLVER.md's non-entity-routing content into wakil the same way

`note-routing/SKILL.md` already has the "code-owned vs. workspace-owned" split
stated as principle; it doesn't yet carry a *default* for the workspace-owned
half. Add:
   - A worked-example judgment pattern for the kind of hard call `RESOLVER.md`'s
     "Concept vs. Project" section makes (instructional/timeless vs.
     productive/time-bound) — as a template for *how* to reason about this class
     of call, not a fixed answer, since the actual vocabulary (what counts as a
     project scope, etc.) stays genuinely KB-specific.
   - The raw-vs-synthesized split (sources/ vs. meetings/) as a default heuristic
     content-synthesis-adjacent skills can fall back on.
   - Sensitive-content handling as a standing caution (already stated once, generically,
     in this repo's own `CLAUDE.md` principle #10 — extend it into the shipped
     skill catalog so every workspace gets it, not just ones that happen to write
     it into `RESOLVER.md`).
   `RESOLVER.md` keeps the truly workspace-specific content: this KB's own
   decision-order list, its specific concept/project examples, its sensitive-path
   name. Delete the now-fully-duplicated "Linking" section outright.

## Critical files

- `src/wakil/llm/prompts.py` — `build_extraction_prompt` gains entity-schema
  rendering (reuse the rendering approach `build_resolution_prompt` already has
  for `entity_types`).
- `src/wakil/app/ingest_service.py` — `prepare_enrichment`/`_run_extraction` pass
  `load_entity_schemas()` through.
- `src/wakil/skills/note-conformance/SKILL.md` — default page-shape-by-category.
- `src/wakil/skills/transcript/SKILL.md`, `article/SKILL.md`, `text/SKILL.md` —
  default citation instruction.
- `src/wakil/skills/note-routing/SKILL.md` — default judgment pattern for
  concept-vs-project-style calls, raw-vs-synthesized split, sensitive-content
  caution.
- `tests/unit/test_ingest_service.py` / a new `tests/unit/test_prompts.py` case —
  assert the extraction prompt includes required fields for a given type
  regardless of `guides` content (proves the fix is structural, not
  guide-dependent).
- Out of scope for this repo, flagged for the KB owner: rewriting
  `~/Projects/kb/schema.md` and `RESOLVER.md` down to their shrunken form.

## Verification

- Re-run the exact failing case: `uv run wakil -w ~/Projects/kb enrich 1 --force`,
  confirm the proposed meeting note now includes `source`/`decisions`/
  `action-items` and a citation-annotated Compiled Truth (or the new default
  document shape) even with `schema.md` present-but-truncated.
- Regression-test the fix's independence from `schema.md`: temporarily point a
  test workspace at no `schema.md` at all and confirm the defaults alone produce
  a reasonable meeting note shape.
- `uv run pytest` (full suite) and `uv run wakil skills validate`/`lint` after
  skill edits.

## Recommended approach — four parts, same session

### A. Entity schemas get a kb-local override path, mirroring the skills resolver

Today `load_entity_schemas()` (`src/wakil/schema/loader.py`) only ever reads
wakil's own shipped `src/wakil/schema/entities/*.yaml` — no per-workspace
override exists, unlike skills. Give it the same resolver shape as
`src/wakil/skills/resolver.py` (`docs/skill-resolution-specification.md`),
applied per entity-type file instead of per skill-directory:

- Precedence order: `WAKIL_SCHEMA_PATH` (colon-separated, mirrors
