# Shift field-shape authority to wakil's built-in schema; shrink schema.md/RESOLVER.md to genuinely-KB-specific prose

## Context

The prior critical-analysis pass found that `wakil enrich`'s frontmatter/page-shape
gaps versus the legacy skill trace mostly to one thing: `load_workspace_guides()`
caps every guide file at `GUIDE_MAX_CHARS = 4_000` and silently slices — this KB's
`schema.md` is 6,538 chars, and the `### meeting` template (the fields the model
most needed) starts at char 4,191, past the cutoff. A background agent then
confirmed a related fact: `validate_proposal()` **already** validates only against
wakil's own `src/wakil/schema/entities/*.yaml`, never against `schema.md` — the
prose schema is *already* redundant with code for validation purposes, just not
yet for the *extraction prompt*, which still depends on schema.md's raw text to
tell the model what fields to fill in.

The user's proposed shift: stop treating `schema.md` as a second, hand-maintained
copy of field shape (a duplication/drift risk `docs/skill-refactor.md` already
names as a rot source), make wakil's built-in entity schema the sole authority for
field shape and validation, and shrink `schema.md` down to prose that genuinely
doesn't reduce to a schema — naming philosophy, page-shape convention, citation
format. Same question extended to `RESOLVER.md`: fold in the parts that aren't
entity-type routing (already code-owned per `note-routing/SKILL.md`'s own stated
split) into wakil as sensible defaults, leaving only genuinely KB-specific
judgment calls in the workspace file.

Reading both files in full surfaced a useful, unplanned data point: this KB's own
`zz-templates/` has no meeting template at all, and its `transcript-template.md`
doesn't even match `schema.md`'s own `### source` block. There is no single
existing canonical "meeting body shape" anywhere in this KB to preserve — the
legacy skill's Summary/Decisions/Action-Items/Discussion-Notes structure is
undocumented tribal knowledge, informally living in one skill file. That
strengthens the case for wakil establishing its own clean, reasoned default rather
than trying to excavate a "correct" answer that doesn't consistently exist.

## What's already true (no change needed)

- `validate_proposal()` and entity stub creation (`_build_stub_entities`) already
  key entirely off `load_entity_schemas()` (`src/wakil/schema/entities/*.yaml`) —
  zero dependency on `schema.md`.
- `note-routing/SKILL.md` already implements exactly this split for *routing*:
  "entity types are code-owned" (`schema.directory`) vs. "everything else is
  workspace-owned, via RESOLVER.md." The user's proposal extends an
  already-proven pattern from routing to shaping, not a new idea.
- `note-conformance/SKILL.md` already duplicates `RESOLVER.md`'s entire
  "Linking" section (absolute-path-only wikilinks) almost verbatim — that section
  of `RESOLVER.md` is pure redundancy today and can simply be deleted from it,
  no wakil change needed.
- Of `RESOLVER.md`'s 10-item decision order, items 2–3 and 5–9 (person, company,
  project, concept, idea, organization, journal) are *already* code-owned via
  `schema.directory` — confirmed each has a `directory:` in
  `src/wakil/schema/entities/*.yaml`. What's genuinely irreducible: the
  concept-vs-project judgment heuristic, the meetings/ (synthesized) vs. sources/
  (raw) split, sensitive-content flagging, and the archive/inbox fallback.

## Recommended approach — four parts, same session

### A. Entity schemas get a kb-local override path, mirroring the skills resolver

Today `load_entity_schemas()` (`src/wakil/schema/loader.py`) only ever reads
wakil's own shipped `src/wakil/schema/entities/*.yaml` — no per-workspace
override exists, unlike skills. Give it the same resolver shape as
`src/wakil/skills/resolver.py` (`docs/skill-resolution-specification.md`),
applied per entity-type file instead of per skill-directory:

- Precedence order: `WAKIL_SCHEMA_PATH` (colon-separated, mirrors
  `WAKIL_SKILL_PATH`) → `<kb-root>/schema/entities/` → `<user-config>/wakil/
  schema/entities/` → built-in (`src/wakil/schema/entities/`).
- Resolution is **per type-file, whole-file, first-match-wins** — same
  invariant as skills (`skill-resolution-specification.md` §3: no
  inheritance/partial overrides, no merging fields across files). A kb-local
  `person.yaml` fully replaces the built-in one; a kb-local `recipe.yaml` with
  no built-in counterpart just adds a new type. The *set* of available types is
  the union across all roots; the *content* of each type is whichever root's
  file for that type wins.
- Add `wakil schema list`/`wakil schema which <type>` to the existing
  `schema_app` CLI group (`src/wakil/cli/main.py`), mirroring `wakil skills
  list/which`, so the selected source per type is inspectable — the resolver
  spec's own invariant ("the selected source is inspectable") applies here too.
- `validate_proposal()`/`_build_stub_entities` keep working unchanged — they
  already just consume whatever `load_entity_schemas()` returns.

### B. Give extraction the parsed entity schema directly (the core fix)

`build_extraction_prompt` (`src/wakil/llm/prompts.py`) currently receives only
free-text `guides` (schema.md/RESOLVER.md, truncated, unstructured). Unlike
`build_resolution_prompt`, which already takes `entity_types: dict[str,
EntitySchema]` and renders it deterministically, extraction has no structured
view of field shape at all — which is *why* the meeting note came out missing
`source`/`project`/`decisions`/`action-items`: the model was inferring shape from
whatever schema.md prose survived truncation, not from wakil's own schema.

Change `_run_extraction`/`prepare_enrichment` (`ingest_service.py`) to pass
`load_entity_schemas()` through to `build_extraction_prompt`, and render the
relevant type's full field list (name, required/optional, kind) the same way
`_render_related`/the resolution prompt already render structured data — no
truncation risk, since it's rendering parsed fields, not slicing a file. This is
the change that actually fixes frontmatter completeness, independent of anything
schema.md says or how long it is.

### C. Shrink `schema.md` to prose-only; give wakil sensible built-in defaults for it

Once field shape is code-owned, `schema.md`'s job narrows to what doesn't reduce
to YAML: naming conventions (§1), the page-shape convention (§2 — correctly
scoped to *entity* pages, not documents), the citation convention (§3), wikilink
preference (§5). Two things happen together, not sequentially:

1. **This KB's `schema.md` shrinks** to just those sections (KB-owner edit, not a
   wakil change — flagging so it's not lost, but out of scope for this repo).
2. **Wakil's own skills gain sensible defaults** for the same concerns, so a
   workspace with a minimal or absent `schema.md` still behaves well, and a
   present-but-truncated one degrades gracefully instead of losing the *only*
   page-shape guidance the model had:
   - `note-conformance/SKILL.md` gains a default page-shape-by-category rule:
     identity-category → Compiled Truth/Timeline (already implicit in how
     `entity-enrichment`/`note-revision` talk about State+Timeline); document
     category → a Summary/Key-Decisions/Action-Items/Discussion-Notes-style
     default, used when the workspace doesn't specify otherwise.
   - `transcript`/`article`/`text` skills gain a default inline-citation
     instruction (cite claims to their source), overridden by the workspace's
     own format when `schema.md` defines one.
   `schema.md`, still read as today, continues to override these defaults where
   it says something specific — same relationship as now, just far smaller and
   low-stakes if it's ever truncated again, because the part that used to break
   (field shape) no longer depends on it at all.

### D. Fold RESOLVER.md's non-entity-routing content into wakil the same way

`note-routing/SKILL.md` already has the "code-owned vs. workspace-owned" split
stated as principle; it doesn't yet carry a *default* for the workspace-owned
half. Add:
   - A worked-example judgment pattern for the kind of hard call `RESOLVER.md`'s
     "Concept vs. Project" section makes (instructional/timeless vs.
     productive/time-bound) — as a template for *how* to reason about this class
     of call, not a fixed answer, since the actual vocabulary (what counts as a
     project scope, etc.) stays genuinely KB-specific.
   - The raw-vs-synthesized split (sources/ vs. meetings/) as a default heuristic
     content-synthesis-adjacent skills can fall back on.
   - Sensitive-content handling as a standing caution (already stated once, generically,
     in this repo's own `CLAUDE.md` principle #10 — extend it into the shipped
     skill catalog so every workspace gets it, not just ones that happen to write
     it into `RESOLVER.md`).
   `RESOLVER.md` keeps the truly workspace-specific content: this KB's own
   decision-order list, its specific concept/project examples, its sensitive-path
   name. Delete the now-fully-duplicated "Linking" section outright.

## Critical files

- `src/wakil/schema/loader.py` — add root resolution (mirror
  `src/wakil/skills/resolver.py`'s `resolve_roots`/precedence logic) so
  `load_entity_schemas()` merges built-in + user + kb-local type files instead
  of only reading `DEFAULT_SCHEMA_DIR`.
- `src/wakil/cli/main.py` — extend the existing `schema_app` group with
  `list`/`which`, mirroring `skills_app`'s `list`/`which` commands
  (`src/wakil/cli/main.py`'s existing `wakil skills` implementation is the
  pattern to reuse).
- `src/wakil/llm/prompts.py` — `build_extraction_prompt` gains entity-schema
  rendering (reuse the rendering approach `build_resolution_prompt` already has
  for `entity_types`).
- `src/wakil/app/ingest_service.py` — `prepare_enrichment`/`_run_extraction` pass
  `load_entity_schemas()` through.
- `src/wakil/skills/note-conformance/SKILL.md` — default page-shape-by-category.
- `src/wakil/skills/transcript/SKILL.md`, `article/SKILL.md`, `text/SKILL.md` —
  default citation instruction.
- `src/wakil/skills/note-routing/SKILL.md` — default judgment pattern for
  concept-vs-project-style calls, raw-vs-synthesized split, sensitive-content
  caution.
- `tests/unit/test_ingest_service.py` / a new `tests/unit/test_prompts.py` case —
  assert the extraction prompt includes required fields for a given type
  regardless of `guides` content (proves the fix is structural, not
  guide-dependent).
- Out of scope for this repo, flagged for the KB owner: rewriting
  `~/Projects/kb/schema.md` and `RESOLVER.md` down to their shrunken form.

## Verification

- New unit tests for the schema resolver mirroring
  `tests/unit/test_skills_resolver.py`'s coverage: built-in resolves with no
  override; kb-local `person.yaml` overrides built-in; a kb-local-only type
  (no built-in counterpart) is still picked up; `wakil schema which <type>`
  reports the right source.
- Re-run the exact failing case: `uv run wakil -w ~/Projects/kb enrich 1 --force`,
  confirm the proposed meeting note now includes `source`/`decisions`/
  `action-items` and a citation-annotated Compiled Truth (or the new default
  document shape) even with `schema.md` present-but-truncated.
- Regression-test the fix's independence from `schema.md`: temporarily point a
  test workspace at no `schema.md` at all and confirm the defaults alone produce
  a reasonable meeting note shape.
- `uv run pytest` (full suite) and `uv run wakil skills validate`/`lint` after
  skill edits.

1	"""Skill root resolution, discovery, and validation.
2	
3	Implements the search-path algorithm from `docs/skill-resolution-specification.md`:
4	an ordered list of skill roots (an explicit `WAKIL_SKILL_PATH` override, the
5	knowledge-base-local `skills/` directory, the user-level config directory, and
6	the built-in root) is normalized, and the first matching, valid skill
7	directory wins.
8	"""
9	
10	from __future__ import annotations
11	
12	import os
13	import re
14	from pathlib import Path
15	from typing import TYPE_CHECKING
16	
17	import frontmatter
18	from pydantic import ValidationError
19	
20	from wakil.config.registry import config_home
21	from wakil.skills.errors import SkillResolutionError
22	from wakil.skills.models import (
23	    SKILL_API_VERSION,
24	    SOURCE_BUILTIN,
25	    SOURCE_KB_LOCAL,
26	    SOURCE_OVERRIDE,
27	    SOURCE_USER,
28	    ResolutionContext,
29	    ResolvedSkill,
30	    RootIssue,
31	    RootResolution,
32	    SkillMetadata,
33	    SkillRoot,
34	)
35	
36	if TYPE_CHECKING:
37	    from collections.abc import Mapping
38	
39	SKILL_NAME_RE = re.compile(r"^[a-z][a-z0-9]*(-[a-z0-9]+)*$")
40	
41	
42	def validate_skill_name(name: str) -> None:
43	    """Raise if `name` is not a valid lowercase-kebab-case skill name.
44	
45	    Rejecting anything that doesn't match `SKILL_NAME_RE` also blocks path
46	    traversal: `/`, `..`, `.`, uppercase letters, and whitespace can't match.
47	    """
48	    if not SKILL_NAME_RE.match(name):
49	        raise SkillResolutionError(
50	            reason="invalid_name",
51	            message=f"{name!r} is not a valid skill name (expected lowercase kebab-case).",
52	            name=name,
53	        )
54	
55	
56	def parse_skill_path(value: str | None) -> list[Path]:
57	    """Split a `WAKIL_SKILL_PATH`-style value on the platform path separator.
58	
59	    Empty segments are dropped so they can never be mistaken for the current
60	    working directory. Paths are returned un-normalized; normalization
61	    happens in `resolve_roots`.
62	    """
63	    if not value:
64	        return []
65	    return [Path(segment) for segment in value.split(os.pathsep) if segment]
66	
67	
68	def _normalize_root(raw: Path) -> Path:
69	    expanded = os.path.expandvars(str(raw))
70	    return Path(expanded).expanduser().resolve()
71	
72	
73	def resolve_roots(context: ResolutionContext) -> RootResolution:
74	    """Build the ordered, normalized, deduplicated list of usable skill roots.
75	
76	    Never raises. Problems with explicit (`WAKIL_SKILL_PATH`) roots are
77	    reported via `RootResolution.issues`; missing or non-directory default
78	    roots are silently dropped per spec §7.
79	    """
80	    raw_entries: list[tuple[Path, str, bool]] = []
81	    for path in parse_skill_path(context.skill_path):
82	        raw_entries.append((path, SOURCE_OVERRIDE, True))
83	    raw_entries.append((context.kb_root / "skills", SOURCE_KB_LOCAL, False))
84	    raw_entries.append((context.user_skill_root, SOURCE_USER, False))
85	    raw_entries.append((context.builtin_skill_root, SOURCE_BUILTIN, False))
86	
87	    seen: set[Path] = set()
88	    unique_entries: list[tuple[Path, str, bool]] = []
89	    for raw_path, source, explicit in raw_entries:
90	        normalized = _normalize_root(raw_path)
91	        if normalized in seen:
92	            continue
93	        seen.add(normalized)
94	        unique_entries.append((normalized, source, explicit))
95	
96	    roots: list[SkillRoot] = []
97	    issues: list[RootIssue] = []
98	    for normalized, source, explicit in unique_entries:
99	        if not normalized.exists():
100	            if explicit:
101	                issues.append(
102	                    RootIssue(
103	                        root=normalized,
104	                        source=source,
105	                        reason="missing",
106	                        message=f"Skill root {normalized} does not exist.",
107	                    )
108	                )
109	            continue
110	        if not normalized.is_dir():
111	            if explicit:
112	                issues.append(
113	                    RootIssue(
114	                        root=normalized,
115	                        source=source,
116	                        reason="not_a_directory",
117	                        message=f"Skill root {normalized} exists but is not a directory.",
118	                    )
119	                )
120	            continue
121	        roots.append(SkillRoot(path=normalized, source=source))
122	
123	    return RootResolution(roots=roots, issues=issues)
124	
125	
126	def _load_skill(skill_dir: Path, expected_name: str) -> tuple[Path, SkillMetadata]:
127	    if not skill_dir.is_dir():
128	        raise SkillResolutionError(
129	            reason="invalid_directory",
130	            message=f"{skill_dir} is not a directory.",
131	            name=expected_name,
132	            path=skill_dir,
133	        )
134	
135	    manifest = skill_dir / "SKILL.md"
136	    if not manifest.is_file():
137	        raise SkillResolutionError(
138	            reason="invalid_directory",
139	            message=f"{manifest} is missing or is not a readable file.",
140	            name=expected_name,
141	            path=manifest,
142	        )
143	
144	    try:
145	        text = manifest.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
146	    except OSError as exc:
147	        raise SkillResolutionError(
148	            reason="invalid_directory",
149	            message=f"{manifest} could not be read: {exc}",
150	            name=expected_name,
151	            path=manifest,
152	        ) from exc
153	
154	    try:
155	        post = frontmatter.loads(text)
156	    except Exception as exc:
157	        raise SkillResolutionError(
158	            reason="invalid_metadata",
159	            message=f"{manifest} has malformed frontmatter: {exc}",
160	            name=expected_name,
161	            path=manifest,
162	        ) from exc
163	
164	    try:
165	        metadata = SkillMetadata.model_validate(dict(post.metadata))
166	    except ValidationError as exc:
167	        raise SkillResolutionError(
168	            reason="invalid_metadata",
169	            message=f"{manifest} has invalid metadata: {exc}",
170	            name=expected_name,
171	            path=manifest,
172	        ) from exc
173	
174	    if metadata.name != expected_name:
175	        raise SkillResolutionError(
176	            reason="invalid_metadata",
177	            message=(
178	                f"{manifest} declares name {metadata.name!r}, "
179	                f"which does not match its directory name {expected_name!r}."
180	            ),
181	            name=expected_name,
182	            path=manifest,
183	        )
184	
185	    if metadata.skill_api != SKILL_API_VERSION:
186	        raise SkillResolutionError(
187	            reason="unsupported_api",
188	            message=(
189	                f"{manifest} declares skill_api={metadata.skill_api}, "
190	                f"but this wakil only supports skill_api={SKILL_API_VERSION}."
191	            ),
192	            name=expected_name,
193	            path=manifest,
194	        )
195	
196	    return manifest, metadata
197	
198	
199	def resolve_skill(name: str, context: ResolutionContext) -> ResolvedSkill:
200	    """Resolve `name` to its winning skill directory, validating it in the process.
201	
202	    The first root containing a `<name>/` directory is authoritative: if it
203	    is invalid, resolution fails rather than falling back to a lower-precedence
204	    root (spec §9.2).
205	    """
206	    validate_skill_name(name)
207	
208	    root_resolution = resolve_roots(context)
209	    for issue in root_resolution.issues:
210	        if issue.reason == "not_a_directory":
211	            raise SkillResolutionError(
212	                reason="invalid_root",
213	                message=issue.message,
214	                path=issue.root,
215	            )
216	
217	    for root in root_resolution.roots:
218	        skill_dir = root.path / name
219	        if not skill_dir.exists():
220	            continue
221	        manifest, metadata = _load_skill(skill_dir, expected_name=name)
222	        return ResolvedSkill(
223	            name=name,
224	            source=root.source,
225	            root=root.path,
226	            directory=skill_dir,
227	            manifest=manifest,
228	            metadata=metadata,
229	        )
230	
231	    raise SkillResolutionError(
232	        reason="not_found",
233	        message=f"No skill named {name!r} was found in any configured skill root.",
234	        name=name,
235	        searched_roots=[root.path for root in root_resolution.roots],
236	    )
237	
238	
239	def discover_skill_names(context: ResolutionContext) -> list[str]:
240	    """Sorted, deduped candidate skill names found as immediate children of any root.
241	
242	    Does not validate the skills, only enumerates directory names that look
243	    like skill names.
244	    """
245	    names: set[str] = set()
246	    for root in resolve_roots(context).roots:
247	        for child in root.path.iterdir():
248	            if child.is_dir() and SKILL_NAME_RE.match(child.name):
249	                names.add(child.name)
250	    return sorted(names)
251	
252	
253	def find_shadowed_roots(name: str, context: ResolutionContext) -> list[SkillRoot]:
254	    """Roots (in precedence order) where a `<name>/` subdirectory exists.
255	
256	    Existence check only, no validation of the candidate directories.
257	    """
258	    validate_skill_name(name)
259	    return [
260	        root
261	        for root in resolve_roots(context).roots
262	        if (root.path / name).exists()
263	    ]
264	
265	
266	def default_context(
267	    kb_root: Path, *, environ: Mapping[str, str] | None = None
268	) -> ResolutionContext:
269	    """Build the standard `ResolutionContext` for a knowledge base."""
270	    env = environ if environ is not None else os.environ
271	    return ResolutionContext(
272	        kb_root=kb_root,
273	        user_skill_root=config_home() / "skills",
274	        builtin_skill_root=Path(__file__).resolve().parent,
275	        skill_path=env.get("WAKIL_SKILL_PATH"),
276	    )

1	"""Load entity schemas from schema/entities/*.yaml into typed models.
2	
3	The yaml files ship inside the wakil package (extension happens by forking
4	and editing them, not by runtime discovery from a workspace — a decision
5	settled in docs/ingestion-refactor-spec.md). Loading is cached per directory
6	path, so repeated validation during one command parses the files once.
7	"""
8	
9	from functools import lru_cache
10	from pathlib import Path
11	from typing import Literal
12	
13	import yaml
14	from pydantic import BaseModel, Field, ValidationError, model_validator
15	
16	DEFAULT_SCHEMA_DIR = Path(__file__).parent / "entities"
17	
18	FieldKind = Literal["string", "list", "ref", "enum", "date", "bool", "int"]
19	Category = Literal["identity", "document", "hybrid"]
20	
21	
22	class SchemaLoadError(RuntimeError):
23	    pass
24	
25	
26	class FieldSpec(BaseModel):
27	    required: bool = False
28	    kind: FieldKind
29	    values: list[str] | None = None  # enum only
30	    ref_type: str | None = None  # ref only
31	
32	    @model_validator(mode="after")
33	    def _check_kind_options(self) -> "FieldSpec":
34	        if self.kind == "enum" and not self.values:
35	            raise ValueError("enum fields must declare `values`")
36	        if self.kind != "enum" and self.values:
37	            raise ValueError("`values` is only valid on enum fields")
38	        if self.kind != "ref" and self.ref_type:
39	            raise ValueError("`ref_type` is only valid on ref fields")
40	        return self
41	
42	
43	class EntitySchema(BaseModel):
44	    type: str
45	    directory: str | None = None  # canonical directory, None = no single home
46	    category: Category
47	    fields: dict[str, FieldSpec]
48	    # Per-origin additive sub-schemas (source only), keyed by the base
49	    # `origin` enum value.
50	    origins: dict[str, dict[str, FieldSpec]] = Field(default_factory=dict)
51	
52	    @model_validator(mode="after")
53	    def _check_category_conventions(self) -> "EntitySchema":
54	        # The identity/document/hybrid split *is* the name/title rule
55	        # (entity-metadata.md, cross-cutting findings): a schema that
56	        # contradicts its own category is a transcription bug.
57	        if self.category == "identity" and "title" in self.fields:
58	            raise ValueError(f"{self.type}: identity types must not define `title`")
59	        if self.category == "document" and "name" in self.fields:
60	            raise ValueError(f"{self.type}: document types must not define `name`")
61	        if self.category in ("identity", "hybrid"):
62	            spec = self.fields.get("name")
63	            if spec is None or not spec.required:
64	                raise ValueError(f"{self.type}: {self.category} types must require `name`")
65	        return self
66	
67	
68	def load_entity_schemas(schema_dir: Path | None = None) -> dict[str, EntitySchema]:
69	    """All entity schemas keyed by `type`, cached per directory."""
70	    return _load_cached(str((schema_dir or DEFAULT_SCHEMA_DIR).resolve()))
71	
72	
73	@lru_cache(maxsize=8)
74	def _load_cached(schema_dir: str) -> dict[str, EntitySchema]:
75	    directory = Path(schema_dir)
76	    if not directory.is_dir():
77	        raise SchemaLoadError(f"Entity schema directory not found: {directory}")
78	    schemas: dict[str, EntitySchema] = {}
79	    for path in sorted(directory.glob("*.yaml")):
80	        try:
81	            data = yaml.safe_load(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
82	        except yaml.YAMLError as exc:
83	            raise SchemaLoadError(f"{path.name}: invalid yaml: {exc}") from exc
84	        if not isinstance(data, dict):
85	            raise SchemaLoadError(f"{path.name}: expected a mapping at top level")
86	        try:
87	            schema = EntitySchema.model_validate(data)
88	        except ValidationError as exc:
89	            raise SchemaLoadError(f"{path.name}: {exc}") from exc
90	        if schema.type in schemas:
91	            raise SchemaLoadError(f"{path.name}: duplicate schema for type '{schema.type}'")
92	        schemas[schema.type] = schema
93	    if not schemas:
94	        raise SchemaLoadError(f"No entity schemas found in {directory}")
95	    return schemas

2	name: note-conformance
3	description: Audit a note's frontmatter, slug, links, and prose against wakil's schema and output-quality bar, and fix what's mechanical or flag what isn't. Use after drafting or revising a note, or when auditing existing pages for schema/prose drift.

5	---
6	
7	# note-conformance
8	
9	This is a checking skill, not a content-generating one. `content-synthesis` and
10	`note-revision` decide what a note says; `note-conformance` is the pass that
11	verifies the result is shaped correctly before it goes through `kb-commit` —
12	schema-valid frontmatter, a consistent slug, deterministic links, and prose
13	that meets the no-slop bar. Run it on one note at a time; it produces a short
14	list of fixes applied and issues flagged, not a rewrite.
15	
16	## When to use
17	
18	- After drafting a new note or substantially revising an existing one.
19	- Before `kb-commit`, as a last check on anything about to be written to the
20	  knowledge base.
21	- When explicitly asked to audit existing pages for drift (stale frontmatter
22	  casing, mismatched slugs, missing citations).
23	
24	For frontmatter drift across many notes at once, prefer `wakil schema migrate`
25	(below) over hand-editing every file — let the deterministic tool do the
26	mechanical part, and reserve this skill's judgment for what it can't cover.
27	
28	## Procedure
29	
30	- [ ] Step 1: **Run the mechanical pass first.** For the note's entity type,
31	      run `wakil schema migrate --dry-run --type <type>` and read the diff.
32	      Apply it (`--yes` or per-file confirm) before doing anything by hand —
33	      see "Mechanical fixes" below for exactly what this does and doesn't
34	      cover.
35	- [ ] Step 2: **Check the category rule.** Confirm `name:` vs `title:`
36	      matches the entity's schema category — see "Category rule" below. This
37	      is a hard schema error, not a style preference.
38	- [ ] Step 3: **Check the three-part slug.** Filename, H1, and every
39	      wikilink pointing at this note must agree — see "Slug consistency"
40	      below.
41	- [ ] Step 4: **Check links.** Internal cross-references are `[[path]]`
42	      wikilinks using the note's full workspace-relative path; external
43	      links are copied verbatim from their source, never reconstructed. See
44	      "Links" below.
45	- [ ] Step 5: **Check prose against the no-slop bar.** No filler, no hedged
46	      citations, no LLM preamble, no placeholder dates, exact phrasing
47	      preserved where the phrasing is the insight, titles under 60
48	      characters and specific. See "No-slop output bar" below.
49	- [ ] Step 6: **Report, don't silently resolve, what you can't fix.** A fact
50	      with no traceable source, an entity type unknown to the schema, an
51	      ambiguous frontmatter conflict — flag these explicitly rather than
52	      guessing or deleting. See "Deterministic links, uncitable facts"
53	      below.
54	
55	## Mechanical fixes: `wakil schema migrate`
56	
57	`wakil schema migrate` (`src/wakil/app/schema_migrate_service.py`) is the
58	cheap tier only: mechanical fixes a linter could make, not judgment calls.
59	Concretely, per file, it:
60	
61	- renames casing/naming duplicates (`end_date`→`end-date`, `start_date`→
62	  `start-date`, `linkedin-link`→`linkedin`, `authors`→`author`, `link`→`url`),
63	  dropping the old key only when it's an exact duplicate value — a genuine
64	  conflict (both present, different values) is left in place and surfaced,
65	  never silently resolved;
66	- retypes `organization/`-directory files that were declared `type: concept`
67	  back to `type: organization`;
68	- aligns a mechanically re-cased `title` back to an authored-case `name` when
69	  they differ only by casing (guards a title-caser artifact like `1NSP` →
70	  `1nsp` without touching a genuinely different title);
71	- normalizes a quoted `type: "..."` value.
72	
73	It does **not** touch page structure, section shape, exact-phrasing
74	preservation, or title quality — those stay this skill's prose judgment (see
75	"No-slop output bar"). It also never retypes an unknown `type` or resolves an
76	ambiguous rename; those are always left for manual review.
77	
78	Run it with `--dry-run` first and read the diff before applying — this is
79	`wakil`'s own implementation of test-the-sample-before-the-batch discipline:
80	`plan_schema_migration` only proposes (nothing is touched during planning),
81	and `apply_migrations` re-reads each file immediately before writing,
82	skipping any file that changed on disk since the plan was made rather than
83	overwriting it blind. Use `--type <type>` to scope a run to one entity type,
84	`--yes` to apply without per-file confirmation once you've reviewed the plan,
85	and `--commit` to have each type's fixes land as its own `wakil chore: ...`
86	commit.
87	
88	## Category rule: `name:` vs `title:`
89	
90	The identity/document split is enforced in code
91	(`src/wakil/schema/validate.py:62-69`), not by convention — get it wrong and
92	`validate_frontmatter` returns a hard `SchemaError`, not a warning:
93	
94	- **identity** types (e.g. `person`, `company`) use `name:` only. A `title:`
95	  field on an identity type is an error.
96	- **document** types (e.g. `meeting`) use `title:` only. A `name:` field on a
97	  document type is an error.
98	
99	```yaml
100	# identity type (src/wakil/schema/entities/person.yaml) — name only
101	---
102	type: person
103	name: Jane Doe
104	status: active
105	created: 2026-07-16
106	updated: 2026-07-16
107	---
108	```
109	
110	```yaml
111	# document type (src/wakil/schema/entities/meeting.yaml) — title only
112	---
113	type: meeting
114	title: Q3 planning sync
115	date: 2026-07-16
116	created: 2026-07-16
117	---
118	```
119	
120	An `entity_type` the schema doesn't recognize is itself a hard error — don't
121	best-guess a schema for an unfamiliar `type:`; flag it.
122	
123	## Slug consistency
124	
125	A note's slug appears in three places, and all three must be the same
126	lowercase-kebab string:
127	
128	1. the filename (minus `.md`);
129	2. the H1 heading at the top of the note body;
130	3. every `[[wikilink]]` elsewhere in the knowledge base that points at this
131	   note.
132	
133	`slugify()` (`src/wakil/app/ingest_service.py:661`) is the reference
134	implementation wakil itself uses (and `git_service.py` reuses for branch
135	names): lowercase, non-alphanumeric runs collapsed to a single `-`, leading
136	and trailing `-` stripped. Use it as the definition of "correctly slugged,"
137	not a separate hand-rolled rule. A note whose H1 is Title Case, or whose
138	filename and H1 disagree, is a conformance failure — fix the drifting one to
139	match the filename, don't rename the file to match a stray heading.
140	
141	## Links
142	
143	**Internal cross-references** use the wikilink form `[[path]]`, where `path`
144	is the note's full workspace-relative path — never a bare filename, never a
145	title string, and never a path built relative to the linking file (no
146	`../...`). `schema/validate.py`'s `ref` field kind only checks that a
147	reference is a string; resolving it to an actual note is the knowledge
148	base's own `RESOLVER.md` (a workspace-provided file wakil reads, not one it
149	ships) — defer to whatever path/slug convention the open workspace's
150	`RESOLVER.md` states, but the "absolute path from the vault root, never
151	relative" rule itself is non-negotiable regardless of workspace.
152	
153	**External links** are copied verbatim from their source — see "Deterministic
154	links" below.
155	
156	## No-slop output bar
157	
158	Notes are durable artifacts, not chat output:
159	
160	- No filler phrases ("It's worth noting that...", "Interestingly...").
161	- No hedging when a fact is cited — "X is true" per the source, not "X might
162	  be true."
163	- No LLM preamble ("I've created...", "Here's the updated...", "Certainly!").
164	- No placeholder dates ("recently," an unfilled `YYYY-MM-DD`).
165	- Preserve a speaker's exact words rather than paraphrasing when their
166	  phrasing is itself the insight — don't clean up grammar or swap in your
167	  own terminology for a person's own framework or coinage.
168	- Titles are descriptive enough to find in a search result, under 60
169	  characters, not full sentences, and not generic ("Jane Doe, VP Eng at
170	  Acme" not "Person Page").
171	
172	## Deterministic links, uncitable facts
173	
174	Never guess or reconstruct a URL — a wikilink is built from the note's actual
175	path, an external link is copied from the source that supplied it, never
176	composed from a slug or a memory of what the URL "should" be.
177	
178	When a fact has no traceable source, or a link can't be built deterministically,
179	**flag it rather than inventing a citation or silently deleting the fact.**
180	Both failure modes are worse than an honest gap: a fabricated source misleads
181	every future reader, and a deleted fact is knowledge the base quietly loses.
182

input.new_string:
An `entity_type` the schema doesn't recognize is itself a hard error — don't
best-guess a schema for an unfamiliar `type:`; flag it.

## Page shape by category

The category split isn't just `name:`/`title:` — it implies a different body
shape, and using the wrong one is a conformance failure even when frontmatter
validates cleanly:

- **Identity-category** notes (`person`, `company`, and other types whose
  schema requires `name`) accumulate knowledge across many separate sources
  over time. Shape: **Compiled Truth + Timeline**, split by a horizontal
  rule — a synthesized, always-current "what's true now" section on top
  (`entity-enrichment`'s "texture over facts" is what belongs here), an
  append-only, reverse-chronological evidence log at the bottom
  (`note-revision`'s Timeline discipline governs how it grows). Never
  regenerate the top section from only the newest source — see
  `note-revision`'s "clobbering bug."
- **Document-category** notes (`meeting`, and other types whose schema uses
  `title` for a single dated occurrence) describe one occurrence, not an
  accumulating subject. Compiled Truth + Timeline doesn't fit — a Timeline of
  one event is just the event. Default shape instead: a short **Summary**
  (the load-bearing outcomes, cited), **Key Decisions** (or explicitly "none"
  when there were none — omitting the section reads as "not checked," not
  "checked, nothing found"), **Action Items** (matching any `action-items:`
  the frontmatter carries), and **Discussion Notes** for supporting detail
  and any analytical read on why the source mattered.

This is wakil's own default, used whenever the workspace doesn't specify a
page-shape convention of its own. A workspace's `SCHEMA.md` still wins where
it says something explicit — this default exists so a thin, absent, or
truncated `SCHEMA.md` doesn't leave a document-type note with no shape
guidance at all and falling back to the identity-page shape by default,
which is a category error, not a safe fallback.

## Citations

Every non-obvious claim in a note — a figure, a quote, a stated intention,
anything that isn't common knowledge — should carry inline provenance so a
reader can tell what's grounded versus inferred. Wakil's default annotation:
a parenthetical tag naming the kind of provenance — `(observed)`,
`(self-reported)`, `(inferred)`, `(reported: <source>)` — placed at the point
of the claim, not batched into a footnote. Use the workspace's own citation
format instead when its `SCHEMA.md` defines one; the point is that *some*
consistent, checkable annotation exists, not the exact bracket shape.

A note with zero inline provenance markers anywhere is itself a conformance
smell worth flagging, the same way a missing citation on one specific claim
is — durable notes get reread and acted on long after the source context is
gone, so "what does this rest on" needs to survive that gap.

8	
9	You are the routing step. Given a piece of content that's about to become a

11	entry, a meeting record, or a resolved entity — decide **where it goes**:

20	SCHEMA.md   → how the note is shaped   (note-conformance)
21	```
22	
23	Don't reach across it. If you catch yourself drafting frontmatter or
24	deciding section headings, stop — route first, hand off, let
25	`note-conformance` do the shaping.
26	
27	## Two routing authorities, and when each applies
28	
29	Routing has exactly two sources of truth. Never invent a third.
30	
31	1. **Entity types are code-owned.** If the content resolves to an entity
32	   `entity-resolution`/`entity-enrichment` already identified — a person, a
33	   company, a concept, whatever entity schemas this wakil installation
34	   defines — its destination directory is `schema.directory` for that
35	   entity's `type`, as declared in the schema itself (see
36	   `src/wakil/schema/entities/*.yaml`, `directory:` field). This is not a
37	   judgment call. Don't reason about it, don't override it, don't propose an
38	   alternative directory because it "feels" more fitting. If the type is
39	   unknown to the schema loader, that's a hard stop upstream (entity
40	   resolution refuses to guess), not something to route around here.
41	
42	2. **Everything else is workspace-owned, via `RESOLVER.md`.** Raw sources,
43	   synthesized notes, journal entries, meeting records, and anything else
44	   that isn't a single resolved entity are not wakil's business to place —
45	   they're the knowledge base's own convention. `RESOLVER.md` is one of
46	   wakil's recognized special files (`SPECIAL_FILES` in
47	   `src/wakil/config/settings.py`); when the workspace has one, it is the
48	   **sole authority** for this class of routing decision. Read it, follow
49	   its decision order, and don't second-guess it with judgment imported from
50	   somewhere else.
51	
52	   **If the workspace has no `RESOLVER.md`, or it doesn't cleanly cover the
53	   case in front of you, do not guess a destination. Ask the user.** A wrong
54	   guess here is a misfiled, hard-to-find note; asking costs one question.
55	
56	## Filing principle: primary subject, not format or source
57	
58	When `RESOLVER.md` routes by subject-matter directories (as opposed to a
59	flat "everything of this type goes here" rule), file by the content's
60	**primary subject** — what someone would search for to find this page again
61	— never by its format or where it came from.
62	
63	- An article *about* a company belongs wherever the workspace routes company
64	  material, not in a generic "articles" bucket, because it came from a web
65	  clipping.
66	- A meeting transcript that's substantially about one project belongs with
67	  that project, not filed only under "meetings," because a transcript is a
68	  format, not a subject.
69	- Don't file a document under a workspace's raw-import bucket just because
70	  ingestion happened to produce it there; if it has a clear primary subject,
71	  route it to that subject's home per `RESOLVER.md`.
72

76	problem) and genuinely doesn't fit any subject directory: filing it by topic
77	loses the "this is a synthesis of that one thing" dimension, and filing it
78	by subject muddles it with the subject's own canonical material. Route this
79	narrow case only if the workspace's `RESOLVER.md` actually defines a home
80	for it — don't invent a synthesis-output directory that isn't backed by the
81	workspace's own convention.

84

86	opposed to filing content that references an existing one):
87

89	> with this person again, or are they relevant to your work/interests? Is

98	that's a signal to send it back rather than file it.

103	      output of `entity-resolution`/`entity-enrichment`, with a known

input.new_string:
## Default judgment patterns for hard filing calls

`RESOLVER.md`, when present, is the authority for a workspace's specific
vocabulary — which subject directories exist, what counts as sensitive, its
own hard calls. Two judgment *patterns* recur often enough across knowledge
bases that they're worth carrying as a default reasoning template. Apply
them only when the workspace's own `RESOLVER.md` doesn't already settle the
case in front of you — a workspace's own answer always wins over the
default.

**Instructional/timeless vs. productive/time-bound.** Many workspaces
distinguish a concept-like type (a reusable framework or mental model, no
owner, no due date, transferable across contexts) from a project-like type
(a specific, owned, time-bound effort with a status and an execution log).
When content mixes both — a thesis plus its own execution log — split it:
route the timeless part to the concept-like home, the dated execution
tracking to the project-like home, rather than forcing one artifact to serve
both.

**Raw vs. synthesized.** A capture that hasn't been interpreted yet (a
transcript, a clipping — exactly what `wakil ingest` writes under
`sources/`) and a note that synthesizes what it means are different
artifacts even when they're about the same event. Don't route interpretive
content into a `source`-type location just because that's where the raw
material landed, and don't leave raw material uninterpreted in a directory
meant for synthesis.

## Sensitive content

If a workspace routes anything to a directory or entity type it flags as
sensitive (a schema's `sensitive: true` field, or `RESOLVER.md`'s own
sensitive-content section), treat that routing decision itself as sensitive:
don't surface its content in summaries, exports, or shared context without
being explicitly asked. This extends the working agreement every wakil
session already operates under to the routing decision itself, not just
downstream handling of the resulting note.

## Naming defaults

Absent a workspace-specific naming convention in `RESOLVER.md`, use:

- lowercase kebab-case for every filename (`slugify()`,
  `src/wakil/app/ingest_service.py`, is the reference implementation — see
  `note-conformance`'s "Slug consistency");
- a qualifier suffix to disambiguate two entities that would otherwise
  collide on the same slug (`david-liu-acme.md`, `david-liu-example.md`),
  rather than picking one arbitrarily or silently overwriting;
- a leading ISO date (`YYYY-MM-DD-`) for slugs naming a specific dated
  occurrence — a meeting, a journal entry — not for identity- or
  concept-type slugs, which name a subject rather than an occurrence.

content.text:
## Summary of implementation

All four parts landed: entity schema resolver with kb-local override (`wakil schema list/which`), extraction now gets wakil's full parsed schema instead of truncated `SCHEMA.md` prose, page-shape/citation defaults migrated into skills, and `RESOLVER.md`'s non-routing content folded into `note-routing`. Full suite: 279 passed, same 19 pre-existing unrelated failures from the concurrent QMD/skills work. Lint clean throughout.

## Fresh critical analysis (re-run against the real bug)

Re-ran `enrich 1 --force` and applied it. All four original bugs plus the deeper analysis's gaps are now fixed — full frontmatter (`source`, `decisions`, `action-items`, `transcript` link), correct entity resolution, and genuinely good inline citations that even distinguish who-said-what within one bullet (`reported: Eleni; metrics reported: Ian via Ed`) — arguably better than the legacy skill's single flat `[Source: ...]` tag repeated on every line.

Two things this run surfaced that I hadn't anticipated:

**1. The model classified this as `type: assessment` (→ `sensitive/assessments/`), not `type: meeting`.** This is a real capability gap the legacy skill *structurally couldn't* have — its Phase 2 template always produces a meeting page, with no sensitivity classifier. This transcript contains "candid third-party assessment... personal career/comp reasoning," which is exactly what this KB's own `RESOLVER.md` §1 says routes to `sensitive/`. Plausibly *more correct* than the legacy output — but it's a judgment call, not something to silently prefer. Worth knowing: re-running `--force` isn't idempotent in *kind*, only in mechanism — a second run classified the same transcript differently than my first (undeclined) run did.

**2. A real bug: frontmatter and body prose disagree about which company this is.** Frontmatter correctly says `company: mosaic-private-markets` (fixed, per Part B). But the body text wikilinks `[[companies/mosaic-app|Mosaic]]` — a *different* company (an internal project-management tool, category: employer) that just happens to share the word "Mosaic." Entity-resolution got it right; extraction's own prose-writing didn't consistently use that same resolution when composing wikilinks.

**3. A real gap in my own Part C fix.** The page-shape-by-category default only reaches the model via a bullet I added to `transcript/SKILL.md` that says *"a meeting note is document-category → Summary/Decisions/Actions."* That's meeting-specific phrasing. `note-conformance` — where the general category rule actually lives — isn't part of `wakil enrich`'s automatic DAG at all (it's a manual/Hermes-driven audit skill, confirmed by re-reading `ingest-source/SKILL.md`'s own DAG description). So when extraction picked `assessment` instead of `meeting` this run, it got zero shape steering and defaulted to Compiled Truth + Timeline. Whether that's actually *wrong* for `assessment` is itself unclear — its fields (`subject`, `period`, `status`) look more like a periodic, accumulating record than meeting's single-occurrence shape, which suggests my identity/document category split is too coarse to drive page-shape by itself; document-category bundles single-occurrence types (meeting) with possibly-accumulating ones (assessment) that the `name:`/`title:` rule doesn't actually distinguish.

Want me to fix #2 (entity-consistency between frontmatter and body) and think through #3 (either generalize the shape hint beyond "meeting," or split the category dimension that drives page-shape from the one that drives `name:`/`title:`) — or would you rather sit with these findings first?

Yes fix #2

RE: #1/#3 - wakil needs to be more nuanced on how it determines something is "sensitive" / "assessment".  let's think through the shape hint of "meetings".  ask me questions to ensure that I understand the problem that you're describing.  It's correct that a "meeting" is a single occurrence type, and that a "timeline" and truth compilation do not make sense; conversely, they do make sense in the context of an assessment.  All that said, I'm just not clear about the problem you're raising.

Run an agent in the background to fix #2 while we discuss the rest of it.
Kicking off the background fix for #2 now, then let's dig into #1/#3.

input.description: Fix entity-link mismatch bug in wakil enrich
input.prompt:
Repo: /Users/ebridges/Projects/wakil (a local-first Python CLI, "wakil", for a personal Markdown knowledge base — read CLAUDE.md at the repo root first for the project's engineering principles: keep it simple, deterministic code over model judgment where possible, never silently rewrite content, fail visibly).

## The bug

`wakil enrich <source-id>` runs a two-step model DAG in `src/wakil/app/ingest_service.py`, `prepare_enrichment()`:
1. **Extraction** (`_run_extraction`) — one model call that produces `ExtractionOutput`, including `proposed_note.markdown` (the full text of a new note, frontmatter + body, written by the model). This runs FIRST.
2. **Entity resolution** (`_run_entity_resolution`) — a second model call that independently decides, for each entity the source touched, whether it matches an EXISTING note (`action: "update"`, with a `target_note_path`), needs a new stub page (`action: "create"`), or should be skipped. This runs SECOND, after extraction, and its results are stored in `proposal.entity_resolutions` (list of `EntityResolution` objects — see `src/wakil/llm/schemas.py`) and used to build `proposal.stub_entities` via `_build_stub_entities()`.

Because these are two independent model calls, they can disagree about which existing page a given entity name refers to — and nothing reconciles them afterward. We observed this concretely: for a transcript mentioning a company called "Mosaic", the knowledge base has TWO different company pages that both contain the string "Mosaic" — `companies/mosaic-app.md` (an unrelated internal tool, `name: Mosaic App`) and `companies/mosaic-private-markets.md` (the actual company being discussed, `name: Mosaic`). In one real run:
- **Entity resolution** correctly resolved "Mosaic" → `action: update`, `target_note_path: companies/mosaic-private-markets.md` — this is reflected correctly in the proposed note's own frontmatter (`company: mosaic-private-markets`).
- **Extraction**, writing the note body independently, wrote the wrong wikilink in the prose: `[[companies/mosaic-app|Mosaic]]` — pointing at the WRONG company page, despite the display text correctly reading "Mosaic".

So the same proposed note ends up internally inconsistent: correct in frontmatter, wrong in body prose. This is exactly the kind of entity-confusion bug the codebase already invests heavily in preventing elsewhere (see `_candidate_entity_notes` in `ingest_service.py`, added earlier this session specifically to fix related-entity retrieval so entity-resolution can find the right page — that fix worked, but doesn't help extraction's independently-written prose).

## The fix (deterministic, no new model call)

Add a deterministic reconciliation pass, consistent with the codebase's existing philosophy (see how `_build_stub_entities` and `validate_proposal` already treat `entity_resolutions` as the authoritative source of truth for entity identity — extraction's own guesses about entity destinations are never trusted over entity-resolution's).

After `proposal.entity_resolutions` is populated (end of `_run_entity_resolution`, after `proposal.stub_entities = _build_stub_entities(config, proposal)`), and only if `proposal.proposed_note` is not None:

1. Build a mapping from entity display name (lowercased) to its **authoritative resolved path**:
   - For `action == "update"`: the path is `resolution.target_note_path`.
   - For `action == "create"`: the path is whatever `_build_stub_entities` actually computed and used for that entity (reuse — don't recompute the slugify logic separately; look at how `_build_stub_entities` builds `path = f"{schema.directory}/{slugify(resolution.name)}.md"`, and note it only adds a stub if the path wasn't already taken/existing — you'll need the same effective path here, which is straightforward since `proposal.stub_entities` already contains `ProposedFile(path=..., ...)` per created entity, in the same order as the `create` actions in `proposal.entity_resolutions` — verify this by reading `_build_stub_entities` carefully, since some `create` resolutions may be skipped there, e.g. if the schema/directory is missing or the path already exists — in which case there is no authoritative path to correct against, so leave those alone).
   - Skip `action == "skip"` entirely — no correction target.
   - Key by `resolution.name` lowercased (exact match only — no fuzzy/alias matching; this is a conservative, exact-match-only fix, matching this codebase's stated aversion to guessing).

2. Scan `proposal.proposed_note.content` for wikilinks of the form `[[path]]` or `[[path|display]]` (this repo's wikilink convention — check `note-conformance/SKILL.md`'s "Links" section and existing regexes in the codebase, e.g. search for how wikilinks are matched/rendered elsewhere, such as `_render_related` in `src/wakil/llm/prompts.py`, for the exact syntax conventions already assumed).

3. For each wikilink found: take its display text (or, if no `|display` part, derive comparable text from the path's slug) and look it up (lowercased, exact match) in the name→path mapping from step 1. If there's a match AND the wikilink's current path differs from the authoritative path, rewrite the wikilink to point at the authoritative path (keep the display text as written). Do this via a plain string/regex rewrite of `proposal.proposed_note.content` — do NOT re-run a model call.

4. If any correction was made, append a message to `proposal.warnings` (a `list[str]` field already on `EnrichmentProposal`) describing what was corrected, e.g. `"Corrected 1 entity link in the proposed note to match entity-resolution's own answer: [[companies/mosaic-app|Mosaic]] -> [[companies/mosaic-private-markets|Mosaic]]"` — this must be visible in the preview, never a silent rewrite (check how `proposal.warnings` already gets surfaced in `src/wakil/ui/console.py`'s `print_enrichment_proposal` to confirm warnings are already shown to the user before confirm; if a warning added here wouldn't be shown, that's a related gap to also fix so the correction is genuinely visible, not silent).

## Where to put this

Add a new small function (something like `_reconcile_entity_links(proposal: EnrichmentProposal) -> None`, mutating `proposal.proposed_note.content` in place, plus appending warnings) in `src/wakil/app/ingest_service.py`, called at the end of `_run_entity_resolution` right after `proposal.stub_entities = _build_stub_entities(config, proposal)`. Keep it small and focused — this is a deterministic string-rewrite pass, not a new architectural layer. Follow existing code style in the file (dataclasses, type hints, no unnecessary abstraction).

## Testing

Add unit test(s) to `tests/unit/test_ingest_service.py` (read the existing tests in that file first for fixture/style conventions — there's a `workspace`/`transcript` fixture, a `FakeClient` that returns scripted JSON responses for the two model calls, and existing enrichment tests like `test_enrichment_analyzes_and_links` to follow as a pattern). At minimum:
- A case reproducing the bug: a proposed_note body containing a wikilink to the WRONG path for an entity that entity-resolution resolved to a DIFFERENT, correct path with the same display name — assert the applied/final content has the corrected link, and that a warning was recorded.
- A case where the wikilink already matches entity-resolution's answer — assert nothing changes and no spurious warning is added.
- A case where a wikilink's display text doesn't match any resolved entity name — assert it's left untouched (don't over-correct).

## Verification

Run `uv run pytest tests/unit/test_ingest_service.py -q` and the full `uv run pytest -q` (there are ~19 pre-existing, unrelated failures in `tests/unit/test_skills_resolver.py` and `tests/integration/test_skills_cli.py` caused by a concurrent, unrelated change to `src/wakil/skills/models.py` from another agent working in this same repo right now — do NOT touch those files or try to fix those failures, they are out of scope and not part of this task; just confirm you haven't added any NEW failures beyond that known set). Run `uv run ruff check` on every file you touch and fix any lint issues. Do not modify skill `.md` files, `prompts.py`, or any file outside `src/wakil/app/ingest_service.py` and `tests/unit/test_ingest_service.py` unless you discover the warnings-visibility gap mentioned above in `src/wakil/ui/console.py`, in which case make the minimal fix there too and say so clearly in your final report.

Good — let me separate this into two things I bundled together in my summary, which is probably what made it unclear.

**Thing 1: the mechanism.** Right now nothing tells the extraction model which body shape to use for a type *other than* `meeting`. The only shape guidance that actually reaches `wakil enrich`'s automatic pipeline is a bullet I hand-wrote into `transcript/SKILL.md` that says, specifically, "a meeting note is document-category → Summary/Decisions/Actions." `note-conformance` — the skill where I put the general category-based rule — never gets loaded during automatic `enrich` at all (confirmed by reading `ingest-source/SKILL.md`'s own description of the DAG: only `transcript`/`text`/`article` + `entity-resolve` run automatically). So when the model picked `assessment` this run, it had *zero* explicit shape instruction from wakil either way. It landed on Compiled Truth + Timeline by inferring it from `SCHEMA.md`'s Page Standard section (which literally says "every important *entity* page," not type-specific) — not because wakil told it "assessment wants this." That it landed correctly this time doesn't mean the mechanism is sound; it means we got lucky once.

**Thing 2: the rule itself.** Separately from whether it reaches the model, I'd written the rule as a strict binary: identity category → Compiled Truth/Timeline, document category → Summary/Decisions/Actions — modeled on the *same* identity/document split that already drives the `name:`/`title:` frontmatter rule. You're right that's wrong, and this run proves it: `assessment` is document-category (it uses `title:`... actually let me not assert that without checking — the point is, whatever its category, it behaves like an accumulating record, not a single occurrence, and my rule would've forced it into the wrong shape if it *had* reached the model). The axis that actually predicts shape is something like "single dated occurrence" vs. "accumulating subject" — which doesn't line up cleanly with identity/document (all identity types accumulate, but document types split both ways).

So: Thing 1 is real and would matter *regardless* of what the correct rule turns out to be — there's currently no reliable delivery path for per-type shape guidance in the automatic pipeline. Thing 2 is that the rule I wrote, if it *had* been delivered, would've been wrong for `assessment`.

Two questions to make sure we're aligned before I propose anything:

1. Does that split — delivery mechanism vs. rule content — match what you were sensing, or were you seeing something else entirely in my original summary?
2. For Thing 1: given we just spent this session making wakil's own YAML schema the authority for *field* shape (replacing prose in `SCHEMA.md`), does it seem right to you that body *shape* should become a similar formal property of each type's schema (like `directory`/`category` already are) rather than another skill-prose bullet — or do you see a reason that should live differently from field shape?

Thing 2: help to better understand what decision you need from me on this.

## Thing 2 first, since it's short

Fair pushback — on reflection I didn't actually pose a decision, I just restated the finding. There isn't a philosophical call I need from you here. The axis (single-occurrence vs. accumulating-subject) is the real dimension; I can work out which bucket most types fall into just by reading their own field lists (`meeting`/`journal`/`reflection` have a single `date`; `assessment`/`person`/`company`/`project`/`concept` have `status`/`period`/`maturity` — accumulating). What I *can't* confidently call from outside your own usage are a few genuinely ambiguous ones:

- **`journal`** — is each entry a closed, single-occurrence record of one day, or does it get added to across a day?
- **`reflection`** — single-occurrence (each reflection is its own artifact, per the dream-cycle convention I saw referenced elsewhere — new slug per edit, never rewritten in place) or accumulating?
- **`idea`** / **`organization`** — same question; `organization` in particular (career-ladder-style reference content) smells like it wants to be *updated in place* rather than logged.

`meta`/`index`/`source` I think are moot — extraction never produces those as a `proposed_note` (source is created deterministically at capture, meta/index are wakil's own doc conventions), so they don't need a shape rule at all. If you'd rather I not wait on this and just make a defensible first-pass call on the ambiguous four, say so — genuinely fine either way, this doesn't block Thing 1.

## Thing 1: coupled vs. decoupled

**Coupled — a `page_shape:` field on each type's own YAML schema**, extending `describe_entity_types_full`'s rendering the same way we just extended it for field lists.

- *For*: one file per type stays the single source of truth; reuses the exact resolver and rendering pipeline we already built twice this session (Part A's kb-local override, Part B's prompt rendering) — genuinely close to free given what's already there.
- *Against*: the schema resolver is whole-file-per-type, no partial overrides (same invariant as skills — deliberate, not incidental). So a KB that wants *only* a different shape for `meeting`, keeping every field wakil ships, has to fork and duplicate the entire field list just to change one tag. That's exactly the "two copies that can drift" problem this whole session has been eliminating — just recreated at a smaller scale.

**Decoupled — a template resolved independently, its own kb-local/user/builtin precedence** (a third instance of the same resolver pattern, not a new design).

- *For*: overriding shape doesn't force duplicating fields, or vice versa — they're genuinely separate concerns a KB owner might want to touch independently. Templates can be real markdown prose (headers, example bullets) instead of squeezed into a YAML value.
- *Against*: one more file to know about per type; a template can drift from its schema in its own way (references a field name a schema override later renames, nothing cross-checks it) — the same class of risk, moved rather than eliminated.

**A hybrid that might be the actual answer**: there are only ~2-3 distinct *shapes* across ~10 relevant types, not one shape per type. So decouple the *template prose* (one file per shape — `compiled-truth-timeline.md`, `summary-decisions-actions.md`, wakil-shipped, KB-overridable) from *which shape a type uses* (a small tag, cheap enough to live directly on the schema as a `page_shape:` field without recreating the duplication problem, since it's a single short value, not the thing a KB is actually likely to want to fork independently — "I want a different shape for this one type" is a much rarer edit than "I want my whole document-style shape to look different"). That gets coupling's simplicity for the part that rarely changes alone, and decoupling's reuse for the part that's actual prose and shared across types.

Want me to run with the hybrid, or do you see a reason to fully commit to one side?

- idea: single-ocurrence
- organization: single-occurrence
- meta: single-occurrence
- index: accumulating-subject (I think, open to your take on this)
- source: single-occurrence

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Page-shape templates: narrative body structure, resolved independently of
# field shape so a kb-local override can change just the shape a type uses
# (or just a shape's own template prose) without forking that type's whole
# field list — the same "don't force one override to duplicate the other
# axis" reasoning that keeps skills and entity fields on separate override
# units. Same three-tier precedence (kb-local -> user -> built-in) as entity
# schemas, minus the WAKIL_SCHEMA_PATH override tier — not needed yet; add it
# if a real need shows up.

DEFAULT_TEMPLATE_DIR = Path(__file__).parent / "templates"


def _template_roots(kb_root: Path | None) -> list[SchemaRoot]:
    raw_entries: list[tuple[Path, str]] = []
    if kb_root is not None:
        raw_entries.append((kb_root / "schema" / "templates", SOURCE_KB_LOCAL))
    raw_entries.append((config_home() / "schema" / "templates", SOURCE_USER))
    raw_entries.append((DEFAULT_TEMPLATE_DIR, SOURCE_BUILTIN))

    seen: set[Path] = set()
    roots: list[SchemaRoot] = []
    for raw_path, source in raw_entries:
        normalized = _normalize_root(raw_path)
        if normalized in seen:
            continue
        seen.add(normalized)
        if normalized.is_dir():
            roots.append(SchemaRoot(path=normalized, source=source))
    return roots


def resolve_page_shape_template(shape: str, kb_root: Path | None = None) -> tuple[str, SchemaRoot]:
    """The page-shape template body plus which root won it (whole-file,
    first match wins — same invariant as entity schemas and skills)."""
    for root in _template_roots(kb_root):
        candidate = root.path / f"{shape}.md"
        if candidate.is_file():
            return candidate.read_text(encoding="utf-8"), root
    raise SchemaLoadError(
        f"No page-shape template named {shape!r} found in any of: "
        f"{', '.join(str(r.path) for r in _template_roots(kb_root)) or '(no roots found)'}"
    )

input.content:
Compiled Truth + Timeline — for a note about an accumulating subject: one
that gets touched by multiple, separate sources over time (an identity, or
any other type tracked and updated across its life), not a single dated
occurrence. The two sections have opposite update disciplines and must not
be confused:

- **Compiled Truth** is *re-synthesized* on every update to cover the union
  of what was already known plus whatever's new — never replaced with only
  the newest source's content. This is where texture goes: what the subject
  believes, what it's building, what's driving it — not a bare fact sheet.
- **Timeline / Log** is *append-only, reverse-chronological*. New dated
  entries get added; existing entries — including auto-generated back-link
  lines — are never deleted, rewritten, or reordered.

Skeleton:

```markdown
# {Display Name}

## Compiled Truth

{synthesized, always-current summary — cite non-obvious claims inline}
- {state fields relevant to this subject}

### Open threads
- {what's unresolved}

Cross-references: [[other-entity]]

---

## Timeline / Log

### {date} — source: {kind}
- {what happened / what was learned, cited}
```

input.content:
Single-occurrence record — for a note describing one dated event or
standalone artifact, not an accumulating subject. There is no Timeline: a
running log of one occurrence is just the occurrence restated, so don't use
the Compiled-Truth/Timeline split here.

Not every section below applies to every type using this shape — a meeting
almost always has action items; a reflection or an original idea almost
never does. Include a section only when the source actually supports it;
omit it rather than writing a placeholder like "None" for a section that
doesn't fit the type at all. (For a type like `meeting`, where the section
usually applies but happened not to fire this time, state "None" explicitly
instead of omitting it — that distinguishes "checked, found nothing" from
"not checked.")

Skeleton:

```markdown
# {Title}

## Summary

{the load-bearing outcomes or content, cited}

## Key Decisions

{only for types where deciding something is in scope — e.g. a meeting;
state "None" explicitly if the type usually has this section but didn't
this time}

## Action Items

{only if there are concrete next steps; omit the section entirely if the
type doesn't produce these}

## Discussion Notes

{supporting detail, and any analysis of why this mattered}
```

## Page shape by `page_shape`, not by category

Every entity type declares its own `page_shape:` in its schema file
(`src/wakil/schema/entities/*.yaml`) — a separate axis from `category`.
Using the wrong shape is a conformance failure even when frontmatter
validates cleanly, and `category` is the wrong signal to infer it from:
`category` drives the `name:`/`title:` rule (does this type accumulate an
*identity*), while `page_shape` drives narrative structure (does this type
describe one occurrence or an ongoing subject) — they usually agree but not
always. `organization` and `project` are both `hybrid` category, but
`organization` is `single-occurrence` and `project` is
`compiled-truth-timeline`; check the schema's own `page_shape:` field, don't
re-derive it from category.

The two shapes currently defined (`src/wakil/schema/templates/*.md`):

- **`compiled-truth-timeline`** — for a subject that accumulates knowledge
  across many separate sources over time (`person`, `company`, `project`,
  `concept`, `journal`, `assessment`...). Compiled Truth on top (synthesized,
  always-current — `entity-enrichment`'s "texture over facts" belongs here),
  an append-only Timeline/Log at the bottom (`note-revision`'s Timeline
  discipline governs how it grows). Never regenerate the top section from
  only the newest source — see `note-revision`'s "clobbering bug."
- **`single-occurrence`** — for a note describing one dated event or
  standalone artifact, not an accumulating subject (`meeting`, `reflection`,
  `idea`, `organization`, `meta`, `source`...). No Timeline — a log of one
  occurrence is just the occurrence restated. Summary / Key Decisions /
  Action Items / Discussion Notes, but only the sections that actually apply
  to the type in front of you (a meeting almost always has action items; a
  reflection almost never does — see the template's own guidance on when to
  omit a section versus state "None").

`resolve_page_shape_template()` (`src/wakil/schema/loader.py`) resolves each
shape's template the same kb-local/user/built-in way entity schemas resolve
— but as its *own* override unit (`schema/templates/<shape>.md`, not
`schema/entities/<type>.yaml`), so a workspace can restyle a shape's prose
without forking any type's field list, or repoint a type at a different
shape without touching that shape's template. Both are read directly by
`wakil enrich`'s extraction step now (`build_extraction_prompt` renders the
full catalog), not left to survive `SCHEMA.md` prose truncation.

"""Rich console output: dynamic content must not corrupt through markup parsing.

`console.print(f"...{dynamic}...")` interprets `[...]` in `dynamic` as Rich
markup tags. A wikilink like `[[companies/foo|Bar]]` gets read as nested
tags and silently mangled (reproduced directly against Rich: it renders as
`[]`) rather than raising — the kind of corruption that's easy to miss
because nothing errors, the text just quietly comes out wrong.
"""

from wakil.app.ingest_service import EnrichmentProposal
from wakil.ui.console import console, print_enrichment_proposal


def test_warning_containing_wikilinks_is_not_mangled_by_markup(capsys):
    proposal = EnrichmentProposal(
        source_id=1,
        title="Test",
        warnings=[
            "Corrected 1 entity link in the proposed note to match "
            "entity-resolution's own answer: "
            "[[companies/mosaic-app|Mosaic]] -> "
            "[[companies/mosaic-private-markets|Mosaic]]"
        ],
    )
    console.width = 200  # avoid line-wrapping splitting the assertion text
    print_enrichment_proposal(proposal)
    out = capsys.readouterr().out
    assert "[[companies/mosaic-app|Mosaic]]" in out
    assert "[[companies/mosaic-private-markets|Mosaic]]" in out
    assert "warning: []" not in out

def _deslug(path: str) -> str:
    """Comparable text for a wikilink with no `|display` part: its slug, deslugged."""
    stem = path.strip().rsplit("/", 1)[-1]
    if stem.endswith(".md"):
        stem = stem[:-3]
    return stem.replace("-", " ").replace("_", " ")


def _normalize_link_path(path: str) -> str:
    """A path with any trailing `.md` stripped, for same-target comparison.

    This KB's own wikilinks mix both conventions (`[[people/x]]` and
    `[[sources/y.md]]` both appear for real, valid links) — extraction's
    `.md`-less link and entity-resolution's `target_note_path` (always
    `.md`, matching `Note.path`) can refer to the identical page while
    differing only by this suffix. Only rewrite a link when it points at a
    genuinely different entity, never just to change its extension style.
    """
    stripped = path.strip()
    return stripped[:-3] if stripped.endswith(".md") else stripped

Short answer: it doesn't — not automatically, and this is worth knowing clearly because it's not what the `page_shape` work implies.

I checked `apply_enrichment` (`ingest_service.py:736`) directly:

```python
for proposed in proposed_files:
    target = config.root_path / proposed.path
    if target.exists():
        raise IngestError(f"Refusing to overwrite existing file: {proposed.path}")
    ...
```

**`wakil enrich`'s automatic pipeline is purely additive.** It only ever writes brand-new files (the proposed note + any new entity stubs), and it hard-stops the *entire* apply if any proposed path already exists — there is no code path anywhere in the automatic DAG that edits an existing file's content.

So what does entity-resolution's `action: "update"` actually do, if not update? Two things, both narrow:

1. **Suppresses a redundant stub.** `_build_stub_entities` only builds a stub for `action == "create"` — an `update` resolution just means "don't propose a duplicate page for this entity."
2. **Feeds the link-reconciliation fix from earlier this session.** `_reconcile_entity_links` uses `target_note_path` to correct wikilinks in the *newly proposed* note so they point at the right existing page.

Neither of those touches the existing page itself. And there's a real gap worth flagging: `EntityResolution.proposed_frontmatter` — which the model is explicitly asked to compute for updates ("only the fields that should change," per `entity-resolve/SKILL.md`) — is **produced but never read anywhere in the code.** The model does that work and it's discarded.

So `page_shape` (this session's work) only controls what a *newly created* note looks like — it has nothing to do with update-vs-create. The actual "merge new facts into `people/eleni-karahalios.md`'s existing Compiled Truth, append to her Timeline" work is `note-revision`'s job — and like `note-conformance`, that skill is **not part of the automatic `wakil enrich` DAG**. It's meant to be invoked separately (by you, or by Hermes) after `enrich` runs, using the entity-resolution result as the signal that a page already exists and needs updating.

Practically: if a source mentions someone who already has a page, `wakil enrich` today will correctly *not* duplicate them and will correctly link to them — but nothing in the automatic path actually adds the new information to their page. That's a real hole between "wakil knows this should be an update" and "wakil does the update." Want me to look at what it'd take to close it — e.g., wiring `note-revision` in as a third (optional) DAG step, or exposing a `wakil note update` command that applies `proposed_frontmatter` deterministically for the cases that don't need real judgment?
if wakil knows that an entity should be updated, then wakil should do the update as part of the process (e.g. enrich) -- no need to create a separate command for that at this time.

This is a substantial feature — wakil's first capability that ever modifies an existing file, not just creates new ones. Given the stakes (silently corrupting a real note is much worse than a bad new-file proposal), let me ground the design in what real entity pages actually look like before writing merge code. I just read `eleni-karahalios.md` and `ian-gutwinski.md` in full, and found something important: the real "Compiled Truth" section has **no `## Compiled Truth` heading at all** — it's implicit prose right after the H1. The one reliable anchor in every file is `## Timeline / Log`, plus a trailing block of auto-generated backlink bullets after the dated entries that must never be touched. I'll design the merge around that, not around my template's idealized headers.

Let me check the existing contract/prompt patterns to build this consistently.
